BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r1.claim: Seeking God's pleasure with expenditure stabilizes part of the self against innate love of wealth and reluctance to spend; the soul can be trained despite its natural inclinations.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r1.anchor: جعل بعض أنفسهم ثابتا على الإيمان والطاعة ليزول عنها رذيلة البخل وحب المال

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r2.speaker: البوصيري
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r2.claim: The Burda compares the self to a child: if left alone it grows attached to nursing, but if weaned it can be weaned.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r2.anchor: والنفس كالطفل إن تهمله شب على

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r3.claim: Neglect strengthens idleness and miserliness; imposing difficult bodily and financial worship brings the self into line and purifies it of acquired habits.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r3.anchor: فمتى أهملتها فقد تمرنت واعتادت الكسل والبطالة والبخل وإمساك المال

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r4.claim: The preposition من can mean 'some of,' as in the idiom about shaking some liveliness from one's sleeve.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r4.anchor: فمن تبعيضية كما في قولهم : "هز من عطفه وحرك من نشاطه"

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r5.claim: Wealth counts as part of the self because of the soul's intense attachment to it; giving money stabilizes a part of oneself, while giving life and money gives the whole self.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r5.anchor: إن النفس لشدة تعلقها بالمال كأنه بعض منها فالمال شقيق الروح

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r6.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r6.claim: Rumi's verses distinguish giving money from giving one's life for God and say God repays each with the corresponding gift.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r6.anchor: آن درم دادن سخى را لايق است

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r7.claim: A second reading takes تثبيتا as making something true and firm: spending confirms faith rooted in the heart and confidence that God rewards good action.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التثبيت بمعنى جعل الشيء صادقا محققا ثابتا والمعنى تصديقا

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r8.claim: On this reading من marks the origin of faith in the heart, as in the cited phrase 'envy from themselves.'
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r8.anchor: فمن لابتداء الغاية كما في قوله تعالى : {حسدا من عند أنفسهم}

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r9.claim: A garden on a raised hill enjoys gentle air and protection from hail, yielding better-looking trees and sweeter fruit than low ground with stagnant air.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r9.anchor: مكان مرتفع مأمون من أن يصطلمه البرد

BURSEVI:v1p347/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r1.claim: Some say a productive garden should stand on level ground; rabwa here means soft, fertile soil that swells and grows after rain.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن البستان إذا وقع في موضع مرتفع من الأرض لا تنفعه الأنهار

BURSEVI:v1p347/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r2.claim: He supports this soil reading with the description of earth stirring and swelling after rain.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r2.anchor: فإن المراد من ربوها ما ذكر

BURSEVI:v1p347/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r3.claim: Wābil is heavy rain with large drops and forceful impact; the garden yields its fruit or harvest to its owner or household.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r3.anchor: وصل إليها مطر كبير القطر شديد الوقع

BURSEVI:v1p347/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r4.claim: Akl means the garden's fruit and yield, literally something eaten; ātat can also mean brought forth with aklahā as its sole object.

BURSEVI:v1p347/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r5.claim: The doubled yield is twice the usual crop because of the heavy rain.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r5.anchor: مثلي ما كانت تثمر في سائر الأوقات وذلك بسبب ما أصابها

BURSEVI:v1p347/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v1p347/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says one year's yield equals what another garden produces in two years, so double means a like amount.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r6.anchor: حملت في سنة من الريع ما يحمل غيرها في سنتين

BURSEVI:v1p347/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r7.claim: Another interpretation counts four times the usual crop by taking each double as two times the thing itself.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r7.anchor: ومن فسره بأربعة أمثال ما كانت تثمر حمل الضعف على أصل معناه

BURSEVI:v1p347/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r8.claim: A light drizzle suffices because the soil is excellent and the air mild; sustained drizzle can work like heavy rain.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r8.anchor: المطر الصغير القطر يكفيها لجودتها وكرم منبتها ولطافة هوائها

BURSEVI:v1p347/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r9.claim: An indefinite noun can begin a clause because it answers a conditional, a recognized license for an indefinite subject.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r9.anchor: لوقوعها في جواب الشرط وهو من جملة المسوغات للابتداء بالنكرة

BURSEVI:v1p347/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347/r10.claim: The parable says sincere, strengthening expenditures are pure and never wasted, though their purity varies with intention, like a garden thriving from good soil and rain.
BURSEVI:v1p347/r10.anchor: نفقات هؤلاء الذين ينفقون بسبب ما يحملهم عليه من الابتغاء والتثبيت زاكية عند الله

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r1.claim: The comparison may be distributive: divine favor and standing are the fruit, while large and small donations are heavy and light rain; both increase the result.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التشبيه من قبيل المفرق بأن يشبه زلفاهم من الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r2.claim: God sees sincere work and ostentation, so the verse urges sincerity and warns against showing off.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r2.anchor: لا يخفى عليه شيء وهو ترغيب في الإخلاص مع تحذير عن الرياء

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r3.claim: A discerning worshipper should seek sincerity and freedom from hidden idolatry, since release from it depends on sincere devotion.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r3.anchor: الخلاص عن الطاغوت الخفي وهو الشرك الخفي فإن الخلاص يبتنى على الإخلاص

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r4.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r4.claim: Saʿdī warns that sowing thorns cannot yield flowers, so insincere work will not bear its hoped-for fruit.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r4.anchor: همينست ندت اكر بشنوي كه كر خاركارى

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r5.claim: Pure work is done without wanting anyone to praise its doer; sincerity transforms work and multiplies its reward.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r5.anchor: وخالص الأعمال هو الذي تعملهلا تحب أن يحمدك عليه أحد

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r6.claim: ʿAlī reports from the Prophet that charity speaks five benefits: it grows, is enlarged, turns an enemy into a friend, preserves what would perish, and guards its giver.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r6.anchor: إذا خرجت من يد صاحبها قبل أن تدخل في يد السائل تتكلم بخمس كلمات

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r7.speaker: مكحول الشامي
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r7.claim: Makḥūl says Hell asks leave to prostrate in gratitude when a believer gives charity, since the gift frees a member of Muḥammad's community from punishment.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r7.anchor: إذا تصدق المؤمن بصدقة رضي الله عنه ونادت جهنم يا رب

BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r8.claim: He assigns meanings to charity's letters: ṣād repels harm, dāl guides its giver to Paradise, and qāf signifies nearness to God.
BURSEVI:v1p347#2/r8.anchor: الصدقة تصد وتمنع عن صاحبها مكروه الدنيا والآخرة

QASHANI:2:263-265/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:263-265/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:263-265/r3.claim: The second kind of spending is superior to the first: a garden continues bearing fruit unlike a grain, signifying enduring possession as an acquired quality.
QASHANI:2:263-265/r3.anchor: فضله على الأول بتشبيهه بالجنة، فإن الجنة مع إيتاء أكلها تبقى بحالها

QASHANI:2:263-265/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:263-265/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:263-265/r4.claim: Giving stabilizes the soul in generosity, a divine attribute; the hill signals higher rank, and abundant or light rain signifies abundant or smaller shares of mercy.
QASHANI:2:263-265/r4.anchor: توطينا لها على الجود الذي هو صفة ربانية

QASHANI:2:263-265/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:263-265/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:263-265/r5.claim: God sees the acts and knows which category of giving they belong to.
QASHANI:2:263-265/r5.anchor: بأعمالكم يرى أنها من أي القبيل

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r1.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r1.claim: Asim and Ibn Amir read بربوة with fatḥa on rāʾ in this verse and in al-Mu'minun; Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, Hamza, and al-Kisai use ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ عاصم وابن عامر: بربوة بفتح الراء

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Hasan prefers ربوة with ḍamma and no alif; al-Farisi supports him because its plural is ربى and it derives from rising above the surrounding ground.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r2.anchor: والذي نختار: ربوة، بضم الراء وحذف الألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r3.claim: Riba has a prohibited form—excess in exchanging like weighed or measured goods—and a disliked, non-prohibited form of giving a gift while expecting more back.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r4.claim: In 30:39, gift-riba earns no divine reward like sincere charity; وما آتيتم من ربا may be either a conditional clause or a relative clause, with different grammatical constructions.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p385#2/r4.anchor: وما آتيتم من ربا ليربوا في أموال الناس فلا يربوا عند الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r1.claim: If وما آتيتم من زكاة is a relative clause, its predicate is فأولئك هم المضعفون; the omitted resumptive pronoun is understood, and the discourse shifts from address to third person.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r1.anchor: وقال: وما آتيتم من زكاة ثم قال: فأولئك هم المضعفون

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r2.speaker: عكرمة
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r2.claim: Ikrima explains ولا تمنن تستكثر as forbidding a gift given in order to receive more in return.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r2.anchor: سمعت عكرمة يقول: «ولا تمنن تستكثر» قال: لا تعط شيئا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p387/r3.claim: The nominative تستكثر can describe a future condition or an intended state, but a jussive reading has no semantic fit: the verse does not prohibit giving for the sake of getting more.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r1.claim: For فصرهن in the adjacent bird passage, one interpretation is 'cut them up,' requiring no omitted verb; another is 'incline them,' with إليك attaching to خذ or to the turning verb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r1.anchor: ومن قدر: فصرهن أو فصرهن، أنه بمعنى: قطعهن

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r2.claim: If فصرهن means incline them, Sibawayh's syntax attaches إليك to the nearer verb; attaching it to خذ is also possible, with an object understood for the later verb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r2.anchor: وقياس قول سيبويه: أن يكون متعلقا بقطعهن

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r3.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r3.claim: They lighten the kāf in أكلها when annexed to a feminine noun; Abu Amr alone uses the heavier form for masculine annexes and unannexed forms, while Nafi and Ibn Kathir lighten those too.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r3.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع أكلها [البقرة/ 265] خفيفة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r4.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r4.claim: These readers use a heavy kāf in أكلها, أكل, and أكله; lexical evidence shows أكل can mean edible produce, in contrast to the verbal noun of eating.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p393/r4.anchor: وقرأها عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: أكلها، والأكل، وأكله

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r1.claim: The promise that the garden yields twice its usual produce confirms that أكل here means what is eaten, namely its produce.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r1.anchor: وقوله: فآتت أكلها ضعفين [البقرة/ 265] فيه دلالة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r2.claim: Abu al-Hasan distinguishes أكل as the food eaten from أكل as the act of eating; أَكلة can mean one meal, while اُكلة can mean food.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r2.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: الأكل ما يؤكل، والأكل: الفعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r3.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r3.claim: Abu Zayd says a person described as ذو أكل has a share of worldly livelihood and provision.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p395/r3.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: يقال إنه لذو أكل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p100#2/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p100#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p100#2/r5.claim: The two pronunciations of ربوة, with ḍamma or fatḥa on rāʾ, are both eloquent dialects; the word has seven forms and means elevated ground.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p100#2/r5.anchor: وهما لغتان فصيحتان وفيها سبع لغات وهي ما ارتفع من الأرض وعلا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p102/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p102/r1.claim: The ḍamma reading of أكلها keeps the word's original form; sukūn lightens the word after a possessive suffix and avoids successive ḍammas.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p102/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن ضم أنه أتى بالكلام على أصل ما كان عليه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r3.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r3.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read بربوة with fatḥa on rāʾ, as in al-Muʾminūn; all other readers use ḍamma in both places.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r3.anchor: فقرأ عاصم وابن عامر ﴿ بربوة ﴾ بفتح الراء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r4.claim: These readers lighten and give sukūn to the kāf of أكلها when attached to a feminine noun; Abū ʿAmr alone uses the heavy form with masculine or unpossessed forms.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ﴿ فآتت أكلها ﴾ خفيفة ساكنة الكاف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r5.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r5.claim: These readers use the heavy form of أكلها and related forms throughout the Qurʾān.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p189/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي

QIRAAT-ER:2:265:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:265:17#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:265:17#1/r1.claim: Changing fatḥa to ḍamma on rāʾ gives rubwa instead of rabwa; both dialectal forms mean elevated ground.
QIRAAT-ER:2:265:17#1/r1.anchor: rubwa and rabwa are dialectal variants of the same meaning (elevated ground)

QIRAAT-ER:2:265:22#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:265:22#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:265:22#1/r1.claim: Sukūn on kāf lightens pronunciation while preserving meaning; both forms are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:2:265:22#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: sukūn on kāf (uklahā vs ukulahā). Lighter pronunciation; same meaning

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#3/r1.claim: Qatada explains spending with inner steadfastness as confidence within themselves.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وتثبيتا من أنفسهم ﴾ قال ثقة من أنفسهم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r1.claim: Hasan explains a garden on a rabwa as level ground raised above the water.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ جنة بربوة ﴾ قال هي الأرض المستوية التي تعلو فوق الماء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r2.claim: Mujahid describes the rabwa as elevated, level ground.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد هي الأرض المرتفعة المستوية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#5/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ فطل ﴾ قال الطل الندا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r7.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r7.claim: Al-Khalīl defines ربوة as elevated, fertile land; the word also has variant forms and a cited poem describes rain over its slopes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r7.anchor: الربوة: قال الخليل: أرض مرتفعة طيبة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r1.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash prefers ḍamma in ربوة because the plural الربا is commonly heard; the source rejects al-Suddī’s interpretation as low-lying land and connects the root with increase and height.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r1.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ويختار الضم في ربوة لأنه لا يكاد يسمع في الجمع إلا الربا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r2.claim: Most lexicographers define طل as very light rain; Mujāhid and others extend it metaphorically to dew, and a cited poem mentions dew on a dwelling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p651/r2.anchor: الطل: المستدق من القطر الخفيف، هذا مشهور اللغة. وقال قوم، منهم مجاهد:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r1.claim: The fertile-garden parable contrasts the showy unbeliever with sincere spenders; ابتغاء مرضات الله answers رئاء الناس, while تثبيتا answers lack of faith by describing resolve to preserve the gift from corruption, grounded in certainty of the afterlife.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r2.claim: The same three omitted-subject patterns used for the seed parable apply here: the hypocrites may be likened to a planter, their spending to a seed, or spenders and spending together to seed and planter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r2.anchor: والتقادير الثلاثة التي في قوله: مثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة جارية هنا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects taking ابتغاء as a purpose-object because it coordinates with تثبيتا, and says spending is not done for تثبيت; Makkī calls both purpose complements, which Abū Ḥayyān also rejects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولا يصح أن يكون ابتغاء مفعولا من أجله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r4.claim: ابتغاء and تثبيتا may be circumstantial nouns or purpose complements; تثبيتا is a transitive verbal noun whose omitted object may be God’s reward, making its acquisition a motive for giving.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r4.anchor: وتثبيت، مصدر: ثبت، وهو متعد، ويحتمل أن يكون المفعول محذوفا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r5.speaker: الشعبي، وقتادة، والسدي، وأبو صالح، وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r5.claim: These authorities interpret تثبيتا as certainty: deeply grounded insight strengthens the self to give; Qatāda also explains it as expecting reward, and an anomalous reading تبيينا is cited as support.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p665/r5.anchor: قال الشعبي، وقتادة، والسدي، وأبو صالح، وابن زيد: معناه وتيقنا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r1.speaker: الشعبي والضحاك والكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r1.claim: They gloss تثبيتا as giving zakat while being content with the act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r1.anchor: وقال الشعبي أيضا والضحاك، والكلبي: وتصديقا، أي: يخرجون الزكاة طيبة بها أنفسهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r2.speaker: ابن جبير وأبو مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r2.claim: They understand تثبيتا as confirmation in their religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جبير، وأبو مالك: تحقيقا في دينهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r3.speaker: ابن كيسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r3.claim: He explains it as sincerity and strengthening themselves in obedience through their spending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r3.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: إخلاصا وتوطيدا لأنفسهم على طاعة الله في نفقاتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r4.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r4.claim: He says spenders believe their giving is something for which God will reward them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: ومقرين حين ينفقون أنها مما يثيب الله عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r5.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r5.claim: He also glosses تثبيتا as resolve.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r6.speaker: يمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r6.claim: He also glosses تثبيتا as insight.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r7.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r7.claim: They take تثبيتا to mean that the spenders strengthen themselves; Hasan describes pausing before charity and giving only when it is truly for God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد، والحسن: معناه أنهم يثبتون، أي يضعون صدقاتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r8.claim: He rejects an Egyptian proposal that تثبيتا means intransitive تثبتا: an unmentioned verbal noun cannot be assigned another verb's original construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r8.anchor: ورد هذا القول بأن ذلك لا يكون بالفعل المتقدم على المصدر نحو الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r9.claim: The author distinguishes intransitive ثبت, meaning to become firm, from causative ثبّت, meaning to make firm or establish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r9.anchor: إن ثبت فعل لازم معناه: تمكن، ورسخ، وتحقق. وثبت معدى بالتضعيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r10.claim: He reads the verse as spenders steadying their faith through a difficult act, which humbles the self and makes it yield.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r10.anchor: أنهم يثبتون من أنفسهم على الإيمان بهذا العمل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r11.claim: When the strengthening is attributed to the spenders, min is partitive and governed by the verbal noun; when attributed to the selves, it describes the source of strengthening.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r11.anchor: وإذا كان التثبيت مسندا إليهم كانت: من، في موضع نصب متعلقة بنفس المصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari raises the question of what the partitive min means.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p666/r12.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: فما معنى التبعيض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r1.claim: He says spending for God steadies part of oneself, while giving both wealth and life in God's path steadies all of it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r1.anchor: ومن بذل ماله وروحه معا فهو الذي ثبتها كلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r2.claim: The self itself moves and steadies the giver through its faith and expectation of abundant reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن نفسه هي التي تثبته وتحمله على الإنفاق في سبيل الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r4.claim: The high ground is singled out for its good trees and abundant fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r4.anchor: وخص الربوة لحسن شجرها وزكاء ثمرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r5.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r5.claim: His poem depicts a raised garden between dry heights and thirsty lowlands, watered by itself and bearing fruit at different levels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r5.anchor: كما قال الشاعر، وهو الخليل بن أحمد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r6.claim: He explains rabwa as elevated land without flowing rivers; the author limits this to the particular garden because it receives rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r6.anchor: وتفسير ابن عباس: الربوة، بالمكان المرتفع الذي لا يجري فيه الأنهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r7.claim: The garden depends on rain rather than running water, as was familiar in Arabia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r7.anchor: وخصت بأن سقياها الوابل لا الماء الجاري فيها على عادة بلاد العرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r8.speaker: الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r8.claim: He objects that gardens on high ground lack river water and face winds, while hollows collect water; he instead reads rabwa as fertile earth swelling under rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r8.anchor: فالمراد بالربوة ليس ما ذكروه، وإنما هو كون الأرض طيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r9.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r9.claim: Hasan had already explained rabwa as level ground that does not rise above the water.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r9.anchor: وما قاله قاله قبله الحسن. الربوة الأرض المستوية التي لا تعلو فوق الماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r10.claim: The garden parable contrasts with the first parable: the stone does not benefit from rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p667/r10.anchor: وأنه في مقابلة المثل الأول، والأول لا يؤثر فيه المطر، وهو: الصفوان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r1.claim: He rejects al-Tabari's interpretation of رياض الحزن as gardens of elevated ground; it means gardens of Najd, called al-Hazn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r1.anchor: ولا يراد: برياض الحزن، رياض الربا، كما زعم الطبري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r2.claim: Najd's gardens are praised because their vegetation is more fragrant and their air cooler and finer than Tihama's.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r2.anchor: لأن نباته أعطر، ونسيمه أبرد، وأرق. فهي خير من رياض تهامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r3.claim: They read rabwa with fatḥa on rāʾ, while the other five canonical readers use ḍamma; the same difference occurs at قد أفلح.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر، وعاصم بفتح الراء، وباقي السبعة بالضم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r4.claim: He reads rabwa with kasra on rāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r5.claim: They read برباوة on the pattern of كراهة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر، وأبو عبد الرحمن: برباوة، على وزن: كراهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r6.speaker: أبو الأشهب العقيلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r6.claim: He reads برباوة on the pattern of رسالة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r6.anchor: وأبو الأشهب العقيلي: برباوة، على وزن رسالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r7.claim: أصابها وابل is an adjectival clause for garden, following the fixed location description; it may instead be a circumstantial clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r7.anchor: أصابها وابل جملة في موضع الصفة لجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r8.claim: The wording first gives the lasting feature of being on a high place, then the incidental event of rain; its ordering differs from the stone parable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r8.anchor: وبدىء بالوصف الثابت، وهو: كونها بربوة، ثم بالوصف العارض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r9.claim: آتت means gave, with its recipient omitted; the first object is owner or people and أكل means the edible fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r9.anchor: آتت بمعنى: أعطت، والمفعول الأول محذوف، التقدير: فآتت صاحبها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r10.claim: Ḍiʿfayn is a circumstantial accusative, not a second object; taking آتت to mean produced with one object lacks support in Arabic usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r10.anchor: ونصب: ضعفين، على الحال، ومن زعم أن: ضعفين، مفعول ثان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r11.claim: Fruit is attached to the garden by relation, not ownership; al-ḥamza in الأكل marks the thing eaten.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r11.anchor: والأكل بضم الهمزة الشيء المأكول، وأريد هنا الثمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r12.speaker: الحرميان وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r12.claim: They read ukul with ḍamma on hamza and sukūn on kāf in the described feminine annexation contexts; Abu Amr also transmits a distinction by annexed noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان، وأبو عمرو بضم الهمزة، وإسكان الكاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p668/r13.claim: The remaining readers use the heavier vocalization for ukul.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r1.claim: Ḍiʿfayn may mean twice the normal yield because of rain and the high place, twice other land, or fourfold if a double is taken as two times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r1.anchor: وقيل: ضعفي غيرها من الأرضين، وقيل: أربعة أمثالها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r2.claim: He says the garden yields three times as much; Taj al-Qurra rejects this as having no basis in Arabic and says the doubled yield is one harvest.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r3.speaker: عكرمة وعطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r3.claim: They interpret doubled fruit as two harvests in one year.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r3.anchor: وقال عكرمة، وعطاء: معنى ضعفين أنها حملت في السنة مرتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r4.claim: He suggests ḍiʿfayn can express multiplication rather than exactly twice one yield, meaning many successive multiples, matching the manyfold reward for good deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r4.anchor: بل يكون من التشبيه الذي يقصد به التكثير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r5.speaker: ابن عيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r5.claim: He supplies an omitted clause after the conditional: if rain does not strike it, as in the poetic example where لم تلدني means she did not happen to bear me.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r5.anchor: قال ابن عيسى: فيه إضمار، التقدير: فإن لم يكن يصيبها وابل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r6.claim: On one reading, dew substitutes for heavy rain and the fertile land still yields doubled fruit despite less rainfall.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r6.anchor: والمعنى: أن الطل يكفيها وينوب مناب الوابل في إخراج الثمرة ضعفين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r7.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r7.claim: Alternatively, dew yields less than heavy rain, but still gives some yield and benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r7.anchor: قال الماوردي: زرع الطل أضعف من زرع المطر وأقل ريعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r8.claim: He rejects proposed fronting and postponement as unnecessary and says the Qur'an should not be assigned a poetic license.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r8.anchor: لا حاجة إليها. والتقديم والتأخير من ضرورات الشعر، فينزه القرآن عن ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r9.claim: He identifies the parable's land as Egypt, which thrives without rain and doubles its yield with rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r9.anchor: قال زيد بن أسلم: المضروب به المثل أرض مصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r10.claim: He compares sincere spenders to the garden, and abundant or modest spending to heavy rain or dew; either is accepted when seeking God's face and exerting one's capacity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p669/r10.anchor: فكما أن كل واحد من المطرين يضعف أكل الجنة، فكذلك نفقتهم كثيرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r1.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r1.claim: He compares abundant charity to rain-fed crops and modest charity to dew-fed crops, so a little good should not be abandoned when one cannot give much.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r1.anchor: فلا يدع قليل البر إذا لم يفعل كثيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r2.claim: He compares the growth of sincere gifts, which God nurtures like young livestock, to vegetation on the fertile raised garden, unlike bare stone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r2.anchor: شبه نمو نفقات هؤلاء المخلصين الذين يربي الله صدقاتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r3.speaker: ابن الجوزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r3.claim: He says the sincere believer's expenditure never fails: dew makes the garden good and heavy rain doubles it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r3.anchor: معنى الآية أن صاحب هذه الجنة لا يخيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r4.claim: He parses فطل as the conditional answer with an omitted clause, offering several viable ellipses; the simplest remove one part of a clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r4.anchor: وقوله: فطل، جواب للشرط، فيحتاج إلى تقدير بحيث تصير جملة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r5.claim: A present verb after fa requires an implicit subject, as in the cited verse, so that analysis also needs an omitted clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r5.anchor: متى دخلت الفاء على المضارع فإنما هو على إضمار مبتدأ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r6.claim: A poetic parallel uses a verbless noun phrase after the condition, like the parsing of فطل.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r6.anchor: ألا إن لا تكن إبل فمعزى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r7.speaker: الزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r7.claim: He reads بصير with yāʾ, apparently referring to hypocrites, though the author allows a general reference to everyone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r7.anchor: قرأ الزهري، بالياء، فظاهره أن الضمير يعود على المنافقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r8.claim: The majority read بصير with address to the audience; the shift of address highlights that God knows every deed and intention, promising reward and warning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p670/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالتاء، على الخطاب، وفيه التفات

AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r1.claim: The forms بربوة and برباوة are all Arabic dialects for a high place, from الرابية and the verb ربا يربو.
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم {بربوة} و {بربوة} و {برباوة} و {برباوة} كل من لغات العرب

AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r2.claim: أكل names food, while الأكل can name the act of eating; the poem’s أَكلة and جوعة show the action reading, though aḍḍamma can mean a portion of food.
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r2.anchor: و"الأكل" هو الفعل الذي يكون منك. تقول: "أكلت أكلا"

AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r3.claim: The poet’s أَكلة, with fatḥa, means an act of eating, as reinforced by جوعة in the same line.
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r3.anchor: قال: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد الثامن والأربعون بعد المئة] :

AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p199#2/r4.claim: وابل is heavy rain; Arabic uses both وبَلت and أوبلت as it uses مطرت and أمطرت, and parallel paired forms for dew and rain. The earth is موبولة, while أخذا وبيلا means severe.

FARRA:v1p176/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p176/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p176/r5.claim: In the past conditional فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل, an omitted كان restores the sense; an example and poem show the same ellipsis.
FARRA:v1p176/r5.anchor: أضمرت (كان) فصلح الكلام. ومثله أن تقول: قد أعتقت عبدين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.claim: Spending to seek God’s pleasure means giving in order to obtain His approval.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r1.anchor: أي لطلب رضاه أو طالبين له

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.claim: The phrase strengthening oneself may use min partitivally: spending engages one faculty of the self; giving both wealth and life would engage the whole self.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r2.anchor: فمن تبعيضية كما في قولهم : هز من عطفية وحرك من نشاطه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, min is origination and the omitted object is Islam or confirmation of recompense, rooted in the heart; it may also indicate proving sincerity to other believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r3.anchor: وقد يجعل مفعول تثبيتا محذوفا أي تثبيتا للإسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء من أصل أنفسهم وقلوبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid’s reading tabyīnan, ‘making clear,’ supports interpreting the phrase as showing others one’s sincere faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r4.anchor: ويعضده قراءة مجاهد وتبيينا من أنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī takes min to mean li, so the phrase describes steadying oneself for obedience to God; the author finds this plausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r5.anchor: بمعنى اللام والمعنى توطينا لأنفسهم على طاعة الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.claim: Spending purifies the donor from miserliness and love of wealth, described as a grave disease and root of every sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35#2/r6.anchor: وفيه تنبيه على أن حكمة الإنفاق للمنفق تزكية للنفس عن البخل وحب المال

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r1.claim: A garden on elevated ground has especially attractive trees and wholesome fruit because its air is mild and does not stagnate densely.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r1.anchor: وأعتبر كونها في ربوة لأن أشجار الربى تكون أحسن منظرا وأزكى ثمرا للطافة هوائها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r2.speaker: ابن عامر، عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read rabwa with fatḥ; most read ḍamm, Ibn ʿAbbās reads kasr, and another form is rabāwa.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم بربوة بالفتح والباقون بالضم وابن عباس بالكسر وقرئ رباوة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r3.claim: A variant reads ḥabba, ‘grain,’ instead of janna, ‘garden.’

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r4.claim: The doubled yield may mean repeated abundance, twice the ordinary crop after heavy rain, four times if ḍiʿf means double, or two harvests in one year.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r4.anchor: فالتثنية للتكثير أو مثلي ما كانت تثمر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو، ابن كثير، نافع
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, and Nāfiʿ read the kāf in akl with sukūn as a lightened pronunciation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير ونافع بسكون الكاف تخفيفا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r6.claim: Even light drizzle suffices for a good garden on high ground, so sincere spending never fails to yield reward, though sincerity, effort, love of wealth, and the recipient’s need affect its degree.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r6.anchor: والمراد أن خيرها لا يخلف على حال لجودنها وكرم منبتها ولطافة هوائها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r7.claim: The analogy may be composite, matching pure growing expenditure with a pure fruitful garden under either rain, or differentiated, matching the donors and their small or great gifts with garden and rain.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r8.claim: On the composite analysis the common feature is growth joined with purity; on the differentiated analysis, either the expenditure or the donor is the main comparison, and scholars prefer different constructions.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r8.anchor: وهذا من التشبيه المركب العقلي ولك أن تعتبر تشبيه حال أولئك عند الله تعالى بالجنة على الربوة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r9.claim: God sees every deed and rewards the sincere while warning the ostentatious giver who seeks the gaze of those whose view cannot help, instead of God’s decisive sight.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p36/r9.anchor: فيجازي كلا من المخلص والمرائي بما هو أعلم به ففي الجملة ترغيب للأول وترهيب للثاني

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p97#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p97#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p97#2/r1.claim: Tathbītan min anfusihim means sincere confirmation from themselves.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p97#2/r1.anchor: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} أي تحقيقا من أنفسهم.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p97#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p97#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p97#2/r2.claim: Rabwa means an elevated place, with two pronunciations.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r1.claim: The spenders seek God's pleasure; Qatada glosses 'confirming themselves' as expecting reward, while al-Shabi and al-Kalbi say they give with sincere belief in God's promise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: احتسابا، وقال الشعبي والكلبي: تصديقا من أنفسهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r2.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r2.claim: Ata and Mujahid read the phrase as placing or allocating their wealth; al-Hasan says they proceed with charity only once sure it is for God, holding back if doubt remains.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء ومجاهد: يثبتون أي يضعون أموالهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r3.claim: On this interpretation, tathbit means deliberation, like the related verbal form in the command to devote oneself to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا القول يكون التثبيت بمعنى التثبت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r4.speaker: المبرد والفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Farra say a garden with palms is called janna, while one with grapevines is called firdaus.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r4.anchor: قال (المبرد) (1) والفراء: إذا كان في البستان نخل فهو جنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r5.claim: Ibn Amir and Asim read rabwa with an open ra, while the other readers use a damma; it means level high ground reached by flowing rivers, where plants grow best.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وعاصم بربوة وإلى ربوة في سورة المؤمنون بفتح الراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r6.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr lighten the reading of 'it yielded'; others use a doubled consonant, and Nafi and Ibn Kathir also lighten 'its produce.'
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p327#2/r6.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالتخفيف، وقرأ الباقون بالتثقيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r1.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r1.claim: Ata says the garden produced in one year what another garden yields in two.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r1.anchor: قال عطاء: حملت في السنة من الريع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r2.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r2.claim: Ikrima says it bore fruit twice in one year.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة: حملت في السنة مرتين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r3.claim: Tall means light, gentle rain; al-Suddi identifies it as dew, which falls steadily.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r3.anchor: أي فطش، وهو المطر الضعيف الخفيف ويكون دائما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r4.claim: The garden represents a sincere believer's work: God multiplies a pure giver's charity whether small or large, just as the garden yields with either little or heavy rain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r4.anchor: كذلك يضعف الله صدقة المؤمن المخلص الذي لا يمن ولا يؤذي سواء قلت نفقته أو كثرت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r5.claim: Even continuous light dew does the work of a strong downpour, and God sees what people do.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p328/r5.anchor: وذلك أن الطل إذا كان يدوم يعمل عمل الوابل الشديد

NAHHAS:v1p335/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p335/r1.claim: ابتغاء is purpose accusative and تثبيتا coordinated; readings vary on بربوة; Abu Ishaq says فطل is the dew reaching it.
NAHHAS:v1p335/r1.anchor: مفعول من أجله ( وتثبيتا من أنفسهم ) عطف عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r1.claim: Tathbit min anfusihim may mean strengthening part of themselves in faith, since wealth is kin to the soul and giving wealth steadies part of oneself while giving wealth and life steadies all of it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r1.anchor: ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم } وتثبيتا بعض أنفسهم على الإيمان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r2.claim: Alternatively, it means confirming Islam and confidence in recompense from the core of themselves; spending purifies the donor from miserliness and love of wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r2.anchor: أو تصديقا للإسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء مبتدأ من أصل أنفسهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r3.claim: The elevated garden represents charity, especially zakat; its height improves its appearance and fruit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r3.anchor: أي ومثل نفقة هؤلاء في الزكاة، كمثل بستان بموضع مرتفع

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r4.claim: Ibn Amir and Asim read rabwah with fatḥa; a kasra reading is also reported, and all three vowel forms are dialect variants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم { بربوة } بالفتح وقرىء بالكسر وثلاثتها لغات فيها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr read akl with sukūn as a lightened form; the crop yields twice its usual amount after heavy rain.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r5.anchor: { فأتت أكلها } ثمرتها. وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو بالسكون للتخفيف.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r6.claim: Du'fayn means twice as much, with du'f meaning a like amount; another view takes it as four times the yield.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r6.anchor: { ضعفين } مثلي ما كنت تثمر بسبب الوابل. والمراد بالضعف المثل كما أريد بالزوج الواحد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r7.claim: The accusative is circumstantial, meaning multiplied; if no heavy rain falls, light rain suffices because of the garden's rich soil and cool elevated air.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r7.anchor: { فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل } أي فيصيبها، أو فالذي يصيبها طل، أو فطل يكفيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r8.claim: The parable says sincere donations are accepted and never lost, though their value varies with accompanying circumstances; the garden can represent their standing with God and heavy or light rain their greater or lesser donations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r8.anchor: أن نفقات هؤلاء زاكية عند الله لا تضيع بحال وإن كانت تتفاوت

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r9.claim: God sees people's deeds, warning against show and encouraging sincerity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:265/r9.anchor: تحذير عن الرئاء وترغيب في الإخلاص

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r8.claim: The sincere garden parable is paired by contrast with the showy spender in this verse and by thematic correspondence with the earlier good-spending parable.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r8.anchor: ولما فرغ من مثل العاري عن الشرط ضرب للمقترن بالشرط من الإنفاق مثلا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r1.claim: The sincere spenders seek God's pleasure without worldly or egoistic motives or other defects that would corrupt the deed; marḍāt suggests repeated, enduring satisfaction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r1.anchor: فلذلك صلح كل الصلاح فعري عن المن والأذى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r2.claim: The form marḍāt conveys satisfaction that recurs and persists.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r3.claim: Self-fortification means carefully repairing and purifying one's deeds through patience and restraint; making the soul yield in spending wealth, its close companion, eases other worship, while indulging it strengthens appetite for base desires.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r3.anchor: في إصلاح العمل وإخلاصه بالحمل على الحلم والصفح والصبر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r4.claim: The preposition min is partitive and governs the self as an object, as in the expression to soften someone with one's affection or stir them with one's energy.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r4.anchor: فمن للتبعيض مفعول به مثلها في قولهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r5.claim: The grain parable represents spending in God's path, while the enduring orchard represents spending from the motive of seeking God's pleasure across every good path.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r5.anchor: ومن أنفق ابتغاء لمرضاة الله جعل مثله كالجنة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r6.claim: A garden on a ridge receives sunlight and pollinating winds; a valley garden is less alive because such winds pass over it, and wind is described as the Breath of the All-Merciful.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r6.anchor: في إعلامه أن خير الجنات ما كان في الربوة لتنالها الشمس وتخترقها الرياح اللواقح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r7.claim: The author's preferred sense of double yield is four times the ordinary crop: a double is an amount plus its equal, so two doubles make four, though commentators commonly say twofold.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r8.claim: The parable uses ellipsis by correspondence: the spender named first implies the garden's owner later, while naming the garden implies the omitted expenditure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r8.anchor: ذكر المنفق أولا دال على حذف صاحب الجنة ثانيا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r9.claim: Dew is one subtle stage of rainfall, initially imperceptible; rain progresses from dew to light drizzle, spray, steady rain, downpour, and heavy deluge.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p518/r9.anchor: الطل سن من أسنان المطر خفي لا يدركه الحس حتى يجتمع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r1.claim: Sincere deeds cannot be invalidated, though weak intentions can diminish them; God sees both outward and inward work, so both should be improved.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r1.anchor: أهل هذا الصنف لا يتطرق غلى أعمالهم فساد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.claim: The text presents the unconditioned warning before the positive incentive because preventing harm takes priority over seeking benefit, then returns to warn against boasting and ostentation with a clearer image.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.anchor: وقدم مثل العاري عن الشرط عليه لأن درء المفاسد أولى من جلب المصالح

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r7.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r7.claim: The garden parable represents the believer's deed.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r7.anchor: عن الربيع في الآية قال: هذا مثل ضربه الله لعمل المؤمن

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r8.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r8.claim: Seeking God's pleasure means acting in hope of reward.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r8.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قوله {ابتغاء مرضات الله} قال: احتسابا

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r9.claim: Those who seek God's pleasure do not seek reputation or show.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r9.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لا يريدون سمعة ولا رياء

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r10.speaker: الشعبي
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r10.claim: Thabitan min anfusihim means faith and certainty.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r10.anchor: عن الشعبي {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} قال: تصديقا ويقينا

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r11.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r11.claim: Thabitan min anfusihim means conviction from within themselves.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r11.anchor: عن أبي صالح {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} قال: يقينا من عند أنفسهم

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r12.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r12.claim: Thabitan means carefully considering where to place one's money.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r12.anchor: عن مجاهد {وتثبيتا} قال: يتثبتون أين يضعون أموالهم

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r13.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r13.claim: A person intending charity would pause; he proceeded if it was for God and held back if showmanship intruded.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r13.anchor: عن الحسن قال: كان الرجل إذا هم بصدقة تثبت فإن كان لله أمضى

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r14.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r14.anchor: عن قتادة {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} قال: النية

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas recited rabwa with kasra on the ra; rabwa is elevated ground.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r15.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها {بربوة} بكسر الراء والربوة النشز من الأرض

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r1.claim: A rabwa is level ground that is elevated.
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الربوة الأرض المستوية المرتفعة

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r2.claim: A garden on a rabwa stands on high ground where rivers do not flow.
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {جنة بربوة} قال: المكان المرتفع الذي لا تجري فيه الأنهار

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r3.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r3.claim: Wabil means rain striking the garden.
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل {أصابها وابل} قال: أصاب الجنة المطر

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r4.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r4.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني قال: الوابل الجود من المطر

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r5.claim: The garden yielded double its usual fruit.
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد {فآتت أكلها ضعفين} قال: أضعفت في ثمرها

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r6.claim: As the garden's fruit was doubled, the spender's reward is likewise doubled.
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r6.anchor: عن السدي {فآتت أكلها ضعفين} يقول: كما ضعفت ثمر تلك الجنة فكذلك تضاعف لهذا المنفق ضعفين

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r9.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: الطل: الرذاذ من المطر يعني اللين منه

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r10.claim: The believer's good deed is never lost, just as the garden yields whether it receives heavy rain or dew.
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r10.anchor: عن قتادة قال: هذا مثل ضربه الله لعمل المؤمن يقول: ليس لخيره خلف كما ليس لخير هذه الجنة خلف

DURR-FULL:v2p46/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r11.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r11.claim: He identifies the land as Egypt, where dew produces well and heavy rain doubles the yield.
DURR-FULL:v2p46/r11.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم في قوله {فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل} قال: تلك أرض مصر إن أصابها طل زكت

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r1.claim: Muqatil glosses spending to seek God's pleasure as spending in expectation of reward from Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، قوله ومثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله قال : احتسابا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r2.claim: Al-Rabi says this is a parable God gives for the work of a believer.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r2.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس ، قوله : ومثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله قال : هذا مثل ضربه الله لعمل المؤمن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says such spenders seek God's pleasure and do not seek reputation or to be seen by people.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r3.anchor: سالت الحسن ، عن قوله : ومثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله قال : ينفقون ابتغاء مرضات الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r4.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r4.claim: Al-Sha'bi interprets “as confirmation from themselves” as inward certainty; another report says it means certainty and affirmation, and al-Suddi and Muqatil are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r4.anchor: عن الشعبي وتثبيتا من انفسهم قال : يقينا من انفسهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r5.claim: Mujahid's second interpretation is that the spenders make sure where they place their money.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد وتثبيتا من انفسهم قال : يثبتون اين يضعون اموالهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r6.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Salih, and Maymun ibn Mihran interpret the phrase as choosing the proper recipients or places for zakat.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r6.anchor: وروى عن الحسن وابا صالح ، وميمون بن مهران ، قالوا : مواضع الزكاة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r7.claim: Qatada explains the phrase as spending while expecting reward from God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r7.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : وتثبيتا من انفسهم قال : احتسابا من انفسهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r8.claim: Mujahid says a rabwa is an elevated, level place.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p519/r8.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد 1 قوله : كمثل جنة بربوة قال : الربوه : المكان الظاهر المستوي .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr defines a rabwa as a raised part of the ground; al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Rabi, Ata, and Muqatil are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، قال : الربوة : النشز من الأرض .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r2.claim: Muqatil says the wabil is rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r2.anchor: مقاتل بن حيانفاصابها وابل يقول : اصاب الجنه المطر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r3.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r3.claim: Ata al-Khurasani calls wabil abundant or copious rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r3.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني قال : الوابل : الجود من المطر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r4.claim: Muqatil says “its produce twice over” means the garden bears twice the fruit.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حين قوله : فئاتت اكلها يعني : ثمرتها ضعفين .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r5.claim: Al-Suddi applies the doubled harvest to the spender, whose reward is multiplied twofold.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r5.anchor: عن السدى فئاتت اكلها ضعفين كلما اضعفت ثمر تلك الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says this describes Egyptian land: dew makes it productive, and heavy rain doubles its yield.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r6.anchor: سمعت زيد بن اسلم يقول في قول الله : فان لم يصبها وابل فطل قال : تلك ارض مصر

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses tal as dew; several authorities agree, though al-Rabi calls it a light shower.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قول الله : فان لم يصبها وابل فطل قال : الطل : الندى .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r8.speaker: مقاتل
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r8.claim: Muqatil glosses tal as a fine drizzle of rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r8.anchor: عن مقاتل : فطل يعني بالطل : الرذاذ من المطر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r9.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r9.claim: The garden parable describes a person who spends without seeking reputation or display and does not remind recipients of the gift.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r9.anchor: فهذا مثل من لا ينفق ماله رياء وسمعة ، ولا يمن به على من يعطيه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r10.speaker: جويبر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r10.claim: Juwair calls tal “al-rakk,” then explains that term as gentle rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p520/r10.anchor: قال جويبر ، في قوله : فان لم يصبها وابل فطل قال : الرك من المطر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p522/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p522/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p522/r1.claim: Qatada says this parable teaches that God's promise for the believer's work will not fail, just as the garden's good yield does not fail whether it receives heavy rain or drizzle.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p522/r1.anchor: عن قنادة ، قوله : والله بما تعملون بصير هذا مثل ضربه الله لعمل المؤمن ، يقول : ليس لخبره خلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r1.claim: The sincere spender's garden is set against the show-off spender's image to make the distance between the ranks vivid and renew praise; a more intricate picture beautifies its subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r1.anchor: لزيادة بيان ما بين المرتبتين من البون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r2.claim: The earlier seed image is simple for swiftly picturing multiplied reward; this garden image is more involved because several favorable features enhance the scene and its analogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r2.anchor: ومثله فيما سلف تمثيلا غير كثير التركيب لتحصل السرعة بتخيل مضاعفة الثواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r3.claim: ابتغاء مرضاة الله and تثبيتا are circumstantial accusatives, meaning seeking God's pleasure and strengthening themselves; تثبيت depicts restraining inner hesitation and stinginess.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r4.claim: Repeated practice of difficult virtues makes them firm habits; spending especially strengthens obedience because wealth is precious, and من marks a figurative partiality among states of the self.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p50/r4.anchor: فإن إراضة النفس على فعل ما يشق عليها لها أثر في رسوخ الأعمال حتى تعتاد الفضائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r1.claim: The dual ضعفين indicates repetition rather than exactly two, like لبيك: the garden yields multiplied produce in varying measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r1.anchor: التثنية فيه لمجرد التكرير مثل لبيك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r2.claim: Even without heavy rain, light rain yields a lesser crop; sincere spending brings great reward that varies with sincerity and self-strengthening but never disappoints its giver.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p53/r2.anchor: أي فإن لم يصبها مطر غزير كفاها مطر قليل

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r1.claim: The comparison through كمثل حبة follows the same grammatical analyses as the parable in 2:261.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r1.anchor: إلى قوله: " كمثل حبة " كقوله: مثل الذين ينفقون... كمثل حبة أنبتت سبع

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r2.speaker: الجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r2.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads كمثل حبة, with unpointed ḥāʾ and bāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري " كمثل حبة " بالحاء المهملة والباء.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r3.claim: ابتغاء may be a causal accusative or a circumstantial accusative; تثبيتا coordinates with it under either parse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r3.anchor: قوله: { ابتغآء } فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه مفعول من أجله، وشروط النصب متوفرة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects ابتغاء as causal because تثبيتا is coordinated with it and spending is not done for the sake of confirmation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r4.anchor: منع ابن عطية أن يكون " ابتغاء " مفعولا من أجله، قال: " لأنه عطف عليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r5.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r5.claim: Makkī permits ابتغاء as causal, a view Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls rejected.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r5.anchor: وحكى عن مكي كونه مفعولا من أجله، قال: " وهو مردود بما بيناه "

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r6.claim: If تثبيتا means securing God’s reward from themselves, that reward can motivate spending; if it means making their deeds sincere, a causal reading is unclear.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r6.anchor: فيكون تثبيت الثواب وتحصيله من الله حاملا لهم على النفقة

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies the object as their deeds through sincere intention, and also allows من أنفسهم to function as the object with من meaning ل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r7.anchor: وأبو البقاء قد قدر المفعول المحذوف " أعمالهم بإخلاص النية " ، وجوز أيضا أن يكون

SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r8.claim: من أنفسهم has two analyses: an object through shifted preposition, or an adjective of تثبيتا; تثبيت itself may be transitive or intransitive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265/r8.anchor: وتلخص أن في " من أنفسهم " قولين، أحدهما: أنه مفعول بالتجوز في الحرف،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r1.claim: تثبيتا can be the verbal noun of intransitive تثبت, used in place of التثبت; verbal nouns substitute for one another, as in 73:8, and a reading تثبتا supports this.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r1.anchor: أن التثبيت مصدر تثبت فهو واقع موقع التثبت، والمصادر تنوب عن بعضها.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r2.speaker: ابن رواحة
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r2.claim: Ibn Rawāḥa’s line uses تثبيت with ثبت الله and supports the transitive verb’s verbal-noun usage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن رواحة: 1067 فثبت الله ما أتاك من حسن تثبيت عيسى

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r3.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects substitution unless the corresponding verb is explicitly stated first; otherwise a verbal noun keeps its original verb’s meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r3.anchor: ورد هذا القول بأن ذلك لا يكون إلا مع الإفصاح بالفعل المتقدم على المصدر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r4.claim: He instead distinguishes intransitive ثبت, ‘become firm,’ from causative ثبّت, ‘make firm.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r4.anchor: والذي نقول: إن ثبت - يعني مخففا - فعل لازم معناه تمكن ورسخ، وثبت معدى بالتضعيف،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains partitive من as partial self-commitment: spending wealth steadies part of oneself, while giving life and wealth steadies the whole self.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r5.anchor: معناه أن من بذل ماله لوجه الله فقد ثبت بعض نفسه

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r6.claim: The apparent meaning is that believers’ own faith steadies and moves them to spend; the author therefore favors construing تثبيت as attributed in meaning to themselves.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن نفسه هي التي تثبته وتحمله على الإنفاق في سبيل الله

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r7.claim: If تثبيت is attributed to the spenders, من is an accusative partitive attached to the verbal noun; if attributed semantically to themselves, من also modifies تثبيتا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#2/r7.anchor: فإذا كان التثبيت مسندا إليهم كانت " من " في موضع نصب متعلقة بنفس المصدر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r1.speaker: الخليل
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r1.claim: ربوة is an elevated, fertile tract, derived from ربا يربو, ‘rise’; al-Suddī’s interpretation as low-lying land is wrong.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r1.anchor: والربوة: أرض مرتفعة طيبة، قاله الخليل. وهي مشتقة من ربا يربو أي: ارتفع،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r2.claim: Forms include ربوة and رباوة with three vowelings, plus رابية; the cited poem witnesses روابيه.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r2.anchor: ويقال: ربوة ورباوة بتثليث الراء فيهما، ويقال أيضا: رابية، قال:

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read ربوة with fatḥa; the others use ḍamma.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم " ربوة " بالفتح، والباقون الضم،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r4.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash prefers ḍamma because the plural رباً points to a singular with ḍamma, like برمة/برم and صورة/صور.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r4.anchor: قال الأخفش: " ونختار الضم لأنه لا يكاد يسمع في الجمع إلا الربا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads ربوة with kasra.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r6.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي وأبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r6.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads رياوة and Abū Jaʿfar reads رباوة, alongside other dialect forms.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#3/r6.anchor: والأشهب العقيلي: " رياوة " ، مثل رسالة وأبو جعفر: " رباوة " مثل كراهة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r1.claim: أصابها وابل may be a second adjective of جنة; preferred order puts the stable location before the temporary rain event and commonly places a prepositional phrase before a clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r1.anchor: أحدها: أنها صفة ثانية لجنة، وبدىء هنا بالوصف بالجار والمجرور ثم بالجملة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r2.claim: It may instead modify ربوة, since the garden is part of the elevated tract.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r2.anchor: أن تكون صفة ل " ربوة " ، قال أبو البقاء: " لأن الجنة بعض الربوة "

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r3.claim: A third analysis makes the clause circumstantial from the implicit pronoun inside the prepositional phrase describing the garden.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r3.anchor: أن تكون حالا من الضمير المستكن في الجار لوقوعه صفة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r4.claim: A fourth analysis makes it circumstantial from جنة, now specified by its adjective, with قد understood.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#4/r4.anchor: أن تكون حالا من " جنة " ، وجاز ذلك لأن النكرة قد تخصصت بالوصف،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r1.claim: آتت normally takes two objects, with صاحبها or أهلها omitted as first because the point is what the garden yields and its owner is implied; أكلها is second and ضعفين circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r1.anchor: وهو الأصح أن " آتت " تتعدى لاثنين، حذف أولهما وهو " صاحبها " أو " أهلها ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r2.claim: Treating ضعفين as the second object is a slip and an error.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن " ضعفين " هو المفعول الثاني، وهذا سهو من قائله وغلط.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ analyzes آتت as ‘produced,’ making it a one-object verb; al-Shaykh says that meaning is not known in Arabic, so attributing giving to a garden is metaphorical.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r4.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr read أكلها with ḍamma hamza and still kāf for feminine annexations; Abū ʿAmr’s stated exception concerns masculine or non-pronominal annexations.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو " أكلها " بضم الهمزة وسكون الكاف

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r5.claim: Other readers double the kāf generally; أكل with ḍamma means food and with fatḥa means eating, and it is annexed to the garden as its place or cause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#5/r5.anchor: والأكل بالضم: الشيء المأكول، وبالفتح مصدر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r1.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r1.claim: After conditional fa, the omitted completion may be a predicate: طل is subject of ‘dew falls on it’; an indefinite subject is licensed in a conditional answer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r1.anchor: فذهب المبرد إلى أن المحذوف خبر، وقوله: " فطل " مبتدأ، والتقدير: " فطل يصيبها ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r2.claim: A second parse makes طل predicate of an omitted subject: ‘what falls on it is dew.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r2.anchor: أنه خبر مبتدأ مضمر، أي: فالذي يصيبها طل.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r3.claim: A third, clearest parse makes طل the subject of an omitted verb: ‘dew then falls on it.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r3.anchor: والثالث: أنه فاعل بفعل مضمر تقديره: فيصيبها طل، وهذا أبينها.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r4.claim: Al-Shaykh argues that the third parse deletes the answer clause while retaining one constituent; a present verb after answer-fa needs an omitted subject, as in 5:95.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r4.anchor: والأخير يحتاج فيه إلى حذف الجملة الواقعة جوابا وإبقاء معمول لبعضها،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r5.claim: The author disputes that present-tense verbs after answer-fa necessarily require an implicit subject.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r5.anchor: وفيما قاله نظر، لأنا لا نسلم أن المضارع بعد الفاء الواقعة جوابا يحتاج إلى إضمار مبتدأ.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r6.speaker: امرؤ القيس
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r6.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s phrase فمعزى can be analyzed by the same three parses as فطل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r6.anchor: ونظير الآية قو امرىء القيس: 1069 ألا إن لا تكن إبل فمعزى

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
