SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r7.claim: The proposed inversion that moves fruit-yielding after the conditional is unnecessary: the meaning works already, and normal order is preferred absent necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r7.anchor: وهذا لا حاجة إليه لاستقامة المعنى بدونه، والأصل عدم التقدير والتأخير،

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r8.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r8.claim: Mujāhid glosses طل as dew; the author calls this figurative. طل is fine droplets; طلّه الندى and أطله are used, and its plural is طلال.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r8.anchor: والطل: المستدق من القطر. وقال مجاهد: " هو الندى " وهذا تجوز منه.

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r9.claim: The cited line ولما نزلنا منزلا طله الندى witnesses the verb usage طله.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#6/r9.anchor: ويقال: طله الندى، وأطله أيضا، قال: 1070 ولما نزلنا منزلا طله الندى

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r1.claim: The majority’s خطاب تعلمون shifts from third-person narration to direct address, encouraging sincere spending and deterring ostentation and reputation-seeking.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r1.anchor: قراءة الجمهور: " تعلمون " خطابا وهو واضح، فإنه من الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r2.speaker: الزهري
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads يعلمون in the third person, referring either to the spenders or generally to all people, with spenders included first.
SAMIN-DURR:2:265#7/r2.anchor: والزهري بالياء على الغيبة، ويحتمل وجهين، أحدهما: أن يعود على المنفقين،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.claim: The Qur’an sometimes mentions the opposite of what came before to make the contrast clear; after the empty gifts it presents accepted, fruitful charity, forbidding similar misconduct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r1.anchor: من أساليب فصاحة القرآن أنه يأتي فيه ذكر نقيض ما يتقدم ذكره لتبيين حال التضاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r2.claim: The parable can be parsed as the spending of the spenders being like a planted garden, or as the spender being like a planter of a garden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r2.anchor: وتقدير الكلام ومثل نفقة الذين ينفقون كمثل غراس جنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.claim: Ibtighāʾ means seeking and is an accusative verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial expression; although it could be causal, its coordination with tathbītan makes the verbal-noun reading correct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r3.anchor: وابتغاء معناه طلب، وإعرابه النصب على المصدر في موضع الحال.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r4.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r4.claim: Makkī calls both expressions causal accusatives, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that for tathbītan because spending is not done for the sake of being strengthened.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r4.anchor: وقال مكي في المشكل: كلاهما مفعول من أجله وهو مردود بما بيناه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.speaker: الشعبي والسدي وقتادة وابن زيد وأبو صالح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.claim: They interpret tathbītan as certainty: conviction in their own hearts reinforces them in spending in God’s obedience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r5.anchor: وقال الشعبي والسدي وقتادة وابن زيد وأبو صالح: وتثبيتا معناه وتيقنا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan understand the phrase as checking where to place charity; al-Ḥasan says one gives only if certain it is for God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن: معنى قوله: وتثبيتا أي إنهم يتثبتون أين يضعون صدقاتهم؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the certainty interpretation; the checking interpretation would be expressed by tathabbatan and requires an explicit prior verb to license that unusual verbal noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r7.anchor: والقول الأول أصوب. لأن هذا المعنى الذي ذهب إليه مجاهد والحسن إنما عبارته وتثبتا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r8.claim: Qatāda also glosses tathbītan as generosity or goodness from their own selves; Ibn ʿAṭiyya regards this as close to the first view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358#2/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: وتثبيتا معناه وإحسانا من أنفسهم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r1.claim: A garden is a plot whose trees conceal the ground.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r1.anchor: والجنة البستان وهي قطعة أرض نبتت فيها الأشجار حتى سترت الأرض،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r2.claim: A rabwa is a slight rise with deep, fertile soil, which usually produces better growth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r2.anchor: والربوة ما ارتفع من الأرض ارتفاعا يسيرا معه في الأغلب كثافة التراب وطيبه وتعمقه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r3.claim: He rejects al-Ṭabarī’s identification of Riyāḍ al-Ḥuzn as this sort of garden, explaining that those Najd gardens differ from Tihāma’s and have more fragrant growth and cooler air.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r3.anchor: ورياض الحزن ليس من هذا كما زعم الطبري، بل تلك هي الرياض المنسوبة إلى نجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r4.claim: An Arab woman’s description, “my husband is like Tihāma’s night,” illustrates the region’s oppressive daytime heat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r4.anchor: ولذلك قالت الأعرابية: زوجي كليل تهامة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines a rabwa as elevated land without flowing rivers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الربوة المكان المرتفع الذي لا تجري فيه الأنهار.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s description pertains to this particular garden, since it relies on rainfall, not to every hill; 23:50 describes a raised land with a spring.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r6.anchor: وهذا إنما أراد به هذه الربوة المذكورة في كتاب الله، لأن قوله تعالى: أصابها وابل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the land is level and does not rise above the water, meaning it is not a mountain or a steep slope.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: الربوة الأرض المستوية التي لا تعلو فوق الماء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r8.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r8.claim: Al-Khalīl defines it as elevated, fertile land; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the verse selects a rain-fed location familiar in Arab lands.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r8.anchor: وقال الخليل أرض مرتفعة طيبة وخص الله بالذكر التي لا يجري فيها ماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r9.claim: Al-Suddī reads it as rabāwa, a low place; Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds the expression awkward and derives rabwa from growth and increase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r9.anchor: وقال السدي بربوة أي برباوة وهو ما انخفض من الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r10.speaker: ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r10.claim: They read rabwa with ḍamma on rāʾ; ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir use fatḥa, Ibn ʿAbbās is reported with kasra, and other readers have forms with a lengthened alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r10.anchor: بضم الراء وبها قرأ ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي ونافع وأبو عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r11.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r11.claim: They read rabwa with fatḥa on the rāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r11.anchor: ويقال «ربوة» بفتح الراء وبها قرأ عاصم وابن عامر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r12.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās has kasra on the rāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r12.anchor: ويقال ربوة بكسر الراء وبها قرأ ابن عباس فيما حكي عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r13.claim: They read the variant rabāwa with a lengthened alif after the bāʾ and fatḥa on the initial consonants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r13.anchor: ويقال رباوة بفتح الراء والباء وألف بعدها، وبها قرأ أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الرحمن،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r14.speaker: الأشهب العقيلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r14.claim: Al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads rabāwa with kasra on the rāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r14.anchor: ويقال رباوة بكسر الراء وبها قرأ الأشهب العقيلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r15.claim: Ātat means “yielded”; akl means edible fruit or food, and its possessive ending indicates association, as in a saddle belonging to a mount, not food consumed by the garden.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r16.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r16.claim: They lighten the hamza in akl when attached to a feminine noun; Abū ʿAmr alone differs in specified masculine or unpossessed forms, while ʿĀṣim and the other named readers use the heavy form throughout.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p359/r16.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو «أكلها» بضم الهمزة وسكون الكاف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r1.claim: Akl means food or something eaten, just as ṭaʿma derives from eating; twofold means twice the amount normally expected or gathered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r1.anchor: بمنزلة الطعمة من طعم، أي الشيء الذي يطعم ويؤكل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r2.claim: Even without heavy rain, light drizzle suffices for this fertile garden; ṭall usually means fine light rain, though some call it dew.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others give the common-language meaning of ṭall as light rain; a report from Ibn ʿAbbās also supports dew as an alternative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r3.anchor: قاله ابن عباس وغيره، وهو مشهور اللغة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r4.claim: Some interpret ṭall as dew, a figurative comparison.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r4.anchor: وقال قوم الطل الندى، وهذا تجوز وتشبيه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r5.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies the sense “a light rain is enough for it.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r6.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r6.claim: Others construe the phrase as “the one that fell on it was light rain.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r6.anchor: وقال غيره التقدير فالذي أصابهم طل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r7.claim: The flourishing garden parallels how God nurtures the sincere donors’ charity, like the growth of a young camel described in a report, unlike the bare stone in the preceding parable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r7.anchor: فشبه نمو نفقات هؤلاء المخلصين الذين يربي الله صدقاتهم كتربية الفلو والفصيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r8.claim: God’s seeing all that people do carries both promise and warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r8.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: والله بما تعملون بصير وعد ووعيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r9.speaker: الزهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r9.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads “they do” in the third person, perhaps referring to all people or to the donors specifically; in the latter case it is pure promise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p360/r9.anchor: وقرأ الزهري يعملون بالياء كأنه يريد به الناس أجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r1.claim: The sincere spenders seek God's pleasure.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r2.speaker: الشعبي وقتادة والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r2.claim: “Establishing themselves” means spending with certainty and belief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r2.anchor: أنه الإنفاق على يقين وتصديق وهذا قول الشعبي وقتادة والسدي في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r3.claim: “Establishing themselves” means carefully considering where to place their expenditure.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r3.anchor: أنه التثبيت لارتياد محل الإنفاق فهم ينظرون أين يضعونها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r4.claim: Janna means a garden; Mujahid and Asim al-Jahdari read ḥabba instead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r4.anchor: الجنة البستان وقرأ مجاهد وعاصم الجحدري حبة بالحاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r5.claim: These readers pronounce rabwa with a ḍamma on the rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي بربوة بضم الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r6.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r6.claim: They pronounce rabwa with a fatḥa on the rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r6.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر بفتح الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r7.speaker: الحسن والأعمش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r7.claim: They pronounce the rāʾ in rabwa with a kasra.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو رزين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r8.claim: They read rabāwa with an added alif and a fatḥa; Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Asim al-Jahdari add the alif but use a ḍamma, and variants occur in al-Mu'minun too.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبو رزين برباوة بزيادة ألف وفتح الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r9.claim: Rabwa has three vowel variants and denotes high land with enough water, which yields more than low ground.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r9.anchor: يقال ربوة وربوة وربوة ورباوة والموضع المرتفع من الأرض إذا كان له ما يرويه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r10.claim: Rabwa means elevation; anything elevated and increased is called rabā, including usury in trade.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#4/r10.anchor: الربوة الارتفاع وكل شيء ارتفع وزاد فقد ربا ومنه الربا في البيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r1.claim: They read akulaha with a light, unvowelled kāf everywhere; Abu Amr agrees when the word is attached to a feminine noun, while Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i always use the heavier form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع أكلها والأكل بسكون الكاف حيث وقع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r2.claim: Akul means fruit, and du'fin means twofold.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r2.anchor: وأكلها أي ثمرها ﴿ ضعفين ﴾ أي مثلين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r3.anchor: فأما الظل فقال ابن قتيبة هو أضعف المطر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r4.claim: Tall is continuous, fine rain with small drops that scarcely make water channels run.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r4.anchor: هو المطر الدائم الصغار القطر الذي لا تكاد تسيل منه المثاعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r5.claim: The future form describes a past possibility: if no downpour struck, a light drizzle did; the garden owner and sincere believer are not disappointed by either rain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r5.anchor: وهذا لفظ مستقبل وهو لأمر ماض فمعناه فإن لم يكن أصابها وابل فطل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r6.claim: The garden prospers under light rain or a downpour, just as a sincere believer's giving bears fruit in either case.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r7.speaker: الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r7.claim: Basir means the One who sees; its form fa'il functions like the active participle muf'il.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p319/r7.anchor: والبصير من أسماء الله تعالى معناه المبصر قال الخطابي وهو فعيل بمعنى مفعل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r1.claim: Believers who give seeking God's pleasure do so with conviction that He will reward them fully; this resembles the authenticated report about fasting Ramadan in faith and seeking reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r1.anchor: وهم متحققون مثبتون أن الله سيجزيهم على ذلك أوفر الجزاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r2.speaker: الشعبي، قتادة، أبو صالح، ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī interprets the phrase as affirmation and certainty; Qatāda, Abū Ṣāliḥ, and Ibn Zayd agree, and Ibn Jarīr selects this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r2.anchor: قال الشعبي: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} أي: تصديقا ويقينا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r3.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r3.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan instead say that donors carefully establish where to place their charity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن: أي: يتثبتون أين يضعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r4.speaker: الجمهور، ابن عباس، الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r4.claim: Most commentators define a rabwa as level ground at an elevated place; Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk add that streams run there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r4.anchor: وهو عند الجمهور: المكان المرتفع المستوي من الأرض. وزاد ابن عباس والضحاك: وتجري فيه الأنهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r5.claim: Ibn Jarīr notes three dialectal and recitational forms of rabwa: with ḍamma, common in Medina, the Ḥijāz, and Iraq; fatḥa, used by some Syrians and Kūfans and attributed to Tamīm; and kasra, reported as Ibn ʿAbbās's reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695/r5.anchor: قال ابن جرير: وفي الربوة ثلاث لغات هن ثلاث قراءات: بضم الراء، وبها قرأ عامة أهل المدينة والحجاز والعراق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r1.claim: Wābil is heavy rain, ukul is fruit, and ḍiʿfayn means twice the yield compared with other gardens.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says ṭall is drizzle, a gentle rain; the high garden is sustained by either heavy rain or drizzle, just as a believer's work is never wasted but accepted and multiplied according to the person's deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك: هو الرذاذ، وهو اللين من المطر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r3.claim: God sees everything His servants do, and none of their deeds is hidden from Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p695#2/r3.anchor: لا يخفى عليه من أعمال عباده شيء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r1.claim: Giving wealth, a close companion to life and especially difficult to surrender, disciplines the self, humbles it, restrains desire, and steadies faith and certainty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r1.anchor: وليثبتوا منها ببذل المال الذي هو شقيق الروح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means confirming Islam and the reward from sincere hearts, since spending for God shows genuine belief in recompense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r2.anchor: وتصديقا للإسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء من أصل انفسهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r3.claim: On the first reading, من is partitive, as in ‘he stirred some of his energy’; on the second it marks a starting point, as in envy from within themselves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r3.anchor: وعلى الثاني لابتداء الغاية كقوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r4.claim: Mujahid's reading وتبيينا من أنفسهم supports the interpretation that their spending demonstrates sincere faith to other believers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r4.anchor: وتعضده قراءة مجاهد ( وتبيينا من أنفسهم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r5.claim: Giving wealth establishes a part of oneself, while giving both wealth and life establishes the whole self.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#3/r5.anchor: ومن بذل ماله وروحه معا فهو الذي ثبتها كلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r1.claim: The passage connects steadfastness to striving for God's cause with wealth and selves.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r1.anchor: وتجاهدون في سبيل الله بأموالكم وأنفسكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r2.claim: The givers' expenditure grows in God's regard like a garden on high ground, where trees produce better and finer fruit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r2.anchor: بمكان مرتفع وخصها لأن الشجر فيها ازكى وأحسن ثمرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r3.claim: Wabil means heavy rain, akul means its crop, double means twice the yield, and a light drizzle suffices because the garden's soil is fertile.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r3.anchor: مثلي ما كانت تثمر بسبب الوابل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r4.claim: Alternatively, the people are like the garden, and abundant or modest expenditure is like heavy rain or drizzle; either yields multiplied fruit when spent sincerely and fully.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r4.anchor: أو مثل حالهم عند الله بالجنة على الربوة ونفقتهم الكثيرة والقليلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r5.claim: Readings include كمثل حبة, the word rabwa with three vowel patterns, and أكلها with two dammas.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#4/r5.anchor: وقرىء ( كمثل حبة ) وبربوة ) بالحركات الثلاث وأكلها ) بضمتين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r1.claim: Spending for God's pleasure may mean supporting fighters who defend His religion or helping Muslims who obey Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r1.anchor: يحتمل وجهين : أحدهما : في نصرة أهل دينه من المجاهدين . والثاني : في معونة أهل طاعته من المسلمين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r2.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r2.claim: Al-Shabi, Ibn Zayd, and al-Suddi interpret inner steadfastness as strong conviction and support for the religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r2.anchor: تثبيتا من أنفسهم بقوة اليقين , والنصرة في الدين , وهو معنى قول الشعبي , وابن زيد , والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid understand inner steadfastness as carefully choosing where to place one's alms.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r3.anchor: الثاني : يتثبتون أين يضعون صدقاتهم , قاله الحسن , ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada understand it as seeking reward for themselves with God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r4.anchor: الثالث : يعني احتسابا لأنفسهم عند الله , قاله ابن عباس , وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r5.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r5.claim: Some theologians interpret it as preparing oneself to remain steadfast in obedience to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r5.anchor: والرابع : توطينا لأنفسهم على الثبوت على طاعة الله , قاله بعض المتكلمين .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r6.claim: A rabwa is an elevated place, perhaps level in its elevation, or any ground raised above a watercourse, according to al-Yazidi.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r6.anchor: في الربوة قولان : أحدهما : هي الموضع المرتفع من الأرض , وقيل المستوي في ارتفاعه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r7.speaker: اليزيدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r7.claim: Al-Yazidi defines a rabwa as any land raised above the channel through which water runs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r7.anchor: والثاني : كل ما ارتفع عن مسيل الماء , قاله اليزيدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r8.claim: Wabil can mean heavy rain or abundant rain; Adi ibn Zayd's verse uses it for abundant downpour.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p339/r8.anchor: في الوابل وجهان : أحدهما : المطر الشديد . والثاني : الكثير , قال عدي بن زيد :

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r1.claim: A garden is placed on a rise because its growth is finer and its yield greater; al-Asha's verse illustrates a lush garden drenched by abundant rain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r1.anchor: وإنما خص الربوة لأن نبتها أحسن , وريعها أكثر , قال الأعشى :

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r2.claim: Akl, with a damma on the first letter, means food because it is meant to be eaten.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r2.anchor: والأكل , بالضم : الطعام لأن من شأنه أن يؤكل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r3.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r3.claim: Most interpreters take du'fayn as twofold: the thing plus an equal amount added; another view defines a double as two times the thing.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r3.anchor: لأن ضعف الشيء مثله زائدا عليه , وضعفاه : مثلاه زائدا عليه , وقيل ضعف الشيء مثلاه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r4.claim: Tall means dew, a lesser kind of rain; dew-grown crops are weaker and yield less than rain-grown crops, yet even small charity sustains and benefits.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r4.anchor: الطل : الندى , وهو دون المطر , والعرب تقول : الطل أحد المطرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r5.claim: The parable compares abundant charity to a rain-fed crop and modest charity to a dew-fed crop: do not abandon small charity when unable to give much.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p340/r5.anchor: فأراد بهذا ضرب المثل أن كثير البر مثل زرع المطر كثير النفع , وقليل البر مثل زرع الطل قليل النفع

MUJAHID:v1p116#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p116#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p116#2/r1.claim: Mujahid defines a rabwa as elevated, level ground.
MUJAHID:v1p116#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ بربوة ﴾ الربوة المكان الظاهر المستوي

MUQATIL:2:265/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:265/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:265/r1.claim: The sincere believer spends seeking God's pleasure without reproach; تثبيتا means confirmation of faith in the heart.
MUQATIL:2:265/r1.anchor: وتثبيتا من أنفسهم } ، يعنى وتصديقا من قلوبهم، فهذا مثل نفقة المؤمن التى يريد بها وجه الله عز وجل،

MUQATIL:2:265/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:265/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:265/r2.claim: The elevated garden bears double its fruit when struck by heavy rain, and also yields when it receives only drizzle; so spending for God bears fruit whether much or little.
MUQATIL:2:265/r2.anchor: { كمثل جنة بربوة } ، يعنى بستان فى مكان مرتفع مستو، تجرى من تحتها الأنهار { أصابها } ، يعنى أصاب الجنة { وابل } ،

MUQATIL:2:265/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:265/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:265/r3.claim: Ṭall is light drizzle like dew, and God sees what people spend.
MUQATIL:2:265/r3.anchor: { فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل } ، أى أصابها عطش من المطر، وهو الرذاذ مثل الندى،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r1.claim: Seeking God's approval and تثبيت mean affirming Islam and truly believing in recompense from within oneself; spending evidences sincere faith in reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r1.anchor: أى وتصديقا للاسلام وتحقيقا للجزاء من أصل أنفسهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r2.claim: Min marks the origin of تثبيت, coordinated with the purpose of spending; the likeness concerns the standing of their purified expenditure with God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r2.anchor: ومن لابتداء الغاية وهو معطوف على المفعول له

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r3.claim: A garden on high ground is especially apt because its trees produce purer and better fruit.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r3.anchor: وخصها لأن الشجر فيها أزكى وأحسن ثمرا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r4.speaker: عاصم والشامي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r4.claim: They read the word for high ground as rabwa.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r5.speaker: نافع ومكي وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r5.claim: Their reading gives the word for its produce the vocalization recorded in the source.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r5.anchor: ثمرتها أكلها نافع ومكى و أبو عمرو ﴿ ضعفين ﴾ مثلى ما كانت تثمر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r6.claim: A downpour makes the garden yield twice its previous crop; even a light drizzle suffices because of the excellence of its soil.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r6.anchor: مثلى ما كانت تثمر قبل بسبب الوابل ﴿ فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل ﴾ فمطر صغير القطر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r7.claim: The garden and its rains portray the spenders' large or small expenditures: either is pure and increases their nearness and good standing with God when done for His approval.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r7.anchor: وكما أن كل واحد من المطرين يضعف أكل الجنة فكذلك نفقتهم كثيرة كانت أو قليلة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r8.claim: God sees both the amount spent and the intentions behind it, including any ostentation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p130/r8.anchor: يرى أعمالكم على إكثار وإقلال ويعلم نياتكم فيهما من رياء

ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r2.claim: Those who seek God’s approval give sincerely, affirming that God will reward the spending.
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r2.anchor: أي ينفقونها مقرين أنها مما يثيب الله عليها

ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r3.claim: Rabwa is high ground; janna is a dense, concealing garden, and a watered garden on a rise yields especially well, like sincere charity.

ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r4.claim: Rabwa has four reported forms: with fatḥa, ḍamma, or kasra on rāʾ, and rabāwa.

ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r5.claim: Wabil is heavy rain; akl means fruit, and the alternate reading ukul has the same meaning; ḍiʿfayn means twofold.
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r5.anchor: أي ثمرها، ويقرأ أكلها والمعنى واحد. (ضعفين): أي مثلين

ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r6.claim: Ṭall is persistent fine rain that scarcely makes runoff; ‘if no downpour strikes it, then [it gets] light rain’ supplies an omitted predicate.
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r6.anchor: المطر الدائم الصغار القطر الذي لا يكاد يسيل منه المثاعب

ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r7.claim: ‘God sees what you do’ means He knows it and therefore recompenses it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r7.anchor: أي عليم، وإذا علمه جازى عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r1.claim: Ibtighāʾ is parsed as a purpose complement and tathbītan coordinated with it; Makki treats both as purpose complements, but Ibn Atiyya rejects that analysis for tathbītan because spending is not done for the sake of stabilization.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r1.anchor: قال مكي في المشكل: كلاهما مفعول من أجله. قال ابن عطية: وهو مردود

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya says ibtighāʾ is best read as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially, coordinated with the verbal noun tathbītan; purpose accusative remains possible for ibtighāʾ alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r2.anchor: «ابتغاء» نصب على المصدر في موضع الحال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r3.claim: After warning against corrupt charity, the passage now describes spending that flourishes because it follows the law and its proper intent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r3.anchor: ولما ذكر الله تعالى صفة صدقات القوم الذين لا خلاق لصدقاتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r4.claim: Ibtighāʾ means seeking, and marḍāt is the verbal noun of raḍiya.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r4.anchor: «ابتغاء» معناه طلب. و «مرضات» مصدر من رضي يرضى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r5.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan interpret tathbītan as carefully considering where to place charity; al-Hasan describes giving only after confirming the motive is God's.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r5.anchor: «وتثبيتا» معناه أنهم يتثبتون أين يضعون صدقاتهم قاله مجاهد والحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains tathbītan as belief and certainty; he and Qatada also explain it as seeking God's reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه تصديقا ويقينا قاله ابن عباس. وقال ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة: معناه واحتسابا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r7.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r7.claim: Al-Sha'bi, al-Suddi, Qatada, Ibn Zayd, Abu Salih, and others understand tathbītan as certainty: insightful souls strengthen a person to spend in obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r7.anchor: وقال الشعبي والسدي وقتادة أيضا وابن زيد وأبو صالح وغيرهم: «وتثبيتا» معناه وتيقنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the certainty, reward-seeking, and confirmation readings over al-Hasan and Mujahid because the latter give the verbal noun a nonliteral sense without an explicit preceding verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r8.anchor: وهذه الأقوال الثلاث أصوب من قول الحسن ومجاهد لأن المعنى الذي ذهبا إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya says a verbal noun used in a different sense requires an explicit antecedent verb, as in 71:17 and 73:8.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا لا يسوغ إلا مع ذكر المصدر والإفصاح بالفعل المتقدم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r10.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r10.claim: Al-Nahhas says Mujahid's interpretation would require tathabbatan; Qatada's 'expecting reward' is unfamiliar unless it means that their souls, expecting reward, strengthen them, which he finds far-fetched.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r10.anchor: وقال النحاس: لو كان كما قال مجاهد لكان وتثبتا من تثبت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r11.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r11.claim: Al-Nahhas approves al-Sha'bi's sense: one's own certainty strengthens resolve and judgment to spend in obedience to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r11.anchor: وقول الشعبي حسن، أي تثبيتا من أنفسهم لهم على إنفاق ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r12.claim: Another explanation is that donors acknowledge God will confirm the reward, unlike a hypocrite who does not expect recompense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r12.anchor: وقيل: «وتثبيتا من أنفسهم» أي يقرون بأن الله تعالى يثبت عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r13.claim: A janna is an orchard, a plot whose trees cover it; the word shares the root of jinn and embryo because they are hidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265/r13.anchor: الجنة: البستان، وهي قطعة أرض تنبت فيها الأشجار حتى تغطيها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r1.claim: A rabwa is a slightly elevated place, usually with deep soil and better growth, which explains why it is chosen for the parable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r1.anchor: والربوة: المكان المرتفع ارتفاعا يسيرا، معه في الأغلب كثافة تراب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects al-Tabari's identification with the 'gardens of al-Ḥazn': those are the gardens of Najd, whose growth and air he says are superior to Tihama's.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ورياض الحزن ليست من هذا كما زعم الطبري، بل تلك هي الرياض المنسوبة إلى نجد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r3.claim: An Arab woman compared her husband to a Tihama night, invoked as evidence that Tihama's air is unpleasant except at night.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r3.anchor: وقلما يصلح هواء تهامة إلا بالليل ولذلك قالت الأعرابية:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi reads rabwa as rabāwa, a low-lying place; Ibn Atiyya calls the wording awkward, and the author says it is untenable because the root means increase and elevation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدى: «بربوة» أي برباوة، وهو ما انخفض من الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r5.claim: Al-Farra explains 'a severe seizure' in 69:10 as increased and compares it with taking more than one gave, as evidence for the root's sense of increase.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r6.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r6.claim: Al-Khalil defines rabwa as elevated, good land; the author says the verse pictures a raised place without running water, familiar from Arab experience.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r6.anchor: وقال الخليل: الربوة أرض مرتفعة طيبة وخص الله تعالى بالذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas defines rabwa as elevated land without rivers, inferred from the verse's rainfall; it cannot mean only river-fed land because 11:98 mentions a rabwa with stable water and a spring.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الربوة المكان المرتفع الذي لا تجري فيه الأنهار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r8.claim: In common Arabic, rabwa means any land raised above its surroundings, whether or not water flows there.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r8.anchor: والمعروف من كلام العرب أن الربوة ما ارتفع عما جاوره سواء جرى فيها ماء أو لم يجر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r9.claim: The first four readings are ḍamma for Ibn Kathir, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, Nafi, and Abu Amr; fatḥa for Asim, Ibn Amir, and al-Hasan; kasra for Ibn Abbas and Abu Ishaq; and rabāwa with fatḥa for Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abd al-Rahman.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#2/r9.anchor: وفيها خمس لغات «ربوة» بضم الراء، وبها قرأ ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي ونافع وأبو عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r1.claim: Aṣābah refers to the elevated ground; wābil is heavy rain, and the cited poem describes a luxuriant garden watered by a downpour.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r1.anchor: يعني الربوة. { وابل } أي مطر شديد قال الشاعر:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r2.claim: Ātāt means 'yielded'; ukul is edible fruit, with 14:25 as a parallel; ukla can also mean a bite or two, as in a Muslim report.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r3.claim: The possessive link to the garden is one of association, like a horse's saddle or a house's door, since the garden itself does not eat fruit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r3.anchor: وإضافته إلى الجنة إضافة اختاص، كسرج الفرس وباب الدار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r4.speaker: نافع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r4.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read ukul with a ḍamma on hamza and a still kāf in feminine possessives; Abu Amr lengthens other contexts where the others lighten, while Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i lengthen all listed forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو «أكلها» بضم الهمزة وسكون الكاف،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r5.claim: Akl and ukl mean the same thing.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r6.claim: The garden yields twice the fruit of other land; the author prefers this over the report that it bears twice yearly, meaning one year's yield equals two years elsewhere.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r6.anchor: أي أعطت ضعفي ثمر غيرها من الأرضين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r7.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies an omitted phrase: if no downpour reaches it, a light rain is enough; al-Zajjaj instead glosses the phrase as the light rain that reaches it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r7.anchor: قال المبرد وغيره: تقديره فطل يكفيها. وقال الزجاج: فالذي يصيبها طل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r8.claim: Al-Tall is light, fine rain according to Ibn Abbas and others; Mujahid and some others identify it with dew, which Ibn Atiyya calls figurative comparison.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r8.anchor: والطل: المطر الضعيف المستدق من القطر الخفيف قاله ابن عباس وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r9.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi notes that dew-fed crops yield less than rain-fed crops but retain some growth and benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r9.anchor: قال الماوردي: وزرع الطل أضعف من زرع المطر وأقل ريعا، وفيه وإن قل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r10.claim: Some propose inverted word order, making the garden yield after either heavy rain or drizzle; the author prefers the ordinary order and sees no need for inversion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r10.anchor: قلت: التأويل الأول أصوب ولا حاجة إلى التقديم والتأخير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r11.claim: The parable depicts sincere spending growing as God nurtures charity, like a foal or young camel, unlike dust washed off a bare rock.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r11.anchor: فشبه تعالى نمو نفقات هؤلاء المخلصين الذين يربي الله صدقاتهم كتربية الفلو والفصيل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r12.claim: Al-Ashhab al-Uqayli reads rabāwa with kasra; al-Farra records rabāwa variants and derives them from rising, from rabā yarbū.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#3/r12.anchor: «رباوة» بالكسر، وبها قرأ الأشهب العقيلي. قال الفراء: ويقال برباوة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r1.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that God takes a single date from lawful earnings and nurtures it like a colt or young camel until it becomes mountain-sized or greater; Muslim and the Muwatta transmit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r1.anchor: لا يتصدق أحد بتمرة من كسب طيب إلا أخذها الله بيمينه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r2.claim: God's seeing what people do conveys both promise and warning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والله بما تعملون بصير } وعد ووعيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r3.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r3.claim: Al-Zuhri reads 'they do' in the third person; the pronoun may refer to people generally or just donors, in which case the statement is pure promise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:265#4/r3.anchor: وقرأ الزهري «يعملون» بالياء كأنه يريد به الناس أجمع،

RAZI-FULL:v7p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p48/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v7p48/r4.claim: Al-Qaffāl offers a seed analogy: sincere deeds grow like seed in fertile garden soil, while the reproacher's deed is seed stored on sterile stone and yields nothing when needed.
RAZI-FULL:v7p48/r4.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله تعالى ، وفيه احتمال آخر

RAZI-FULL:v7p48#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p48#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p48#2/r5.claim: The contrasting sincere donors spend for two ends: seeking God's pleasure and تثبيت of themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v7p48#2/r5.anchor: غرض هؤلاء المنفقين من هذا الانفاق أمران

RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r1.claim: Al-Qāḍī says تثبيت means training oneself to preserve obedience and avoid what corrupts it, including subsequent reproach and injury.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r1.anchor: يوطنون أنفسهم على حفظ هذه الطاعة وترك ما يفسدها

RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r2.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r2.claim: Mujāhid's reading, وتثبيتا من بعض أنفسهم, supports construing تثبيت as reassuring others that the donors' faith and sincerity are genuine.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r2.anchor: ويعضده قراءة مجاهد { وتثبيتا من * بعض * أنفسهم }

RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r3.claim: The Kashshāf explains that struggle subdues part of the self attached to worldly life and wealth; spending money stabilizes part, while spending life stabilizes all, as in al-Ṣaff 61:11.

RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī proposes that the heart becomes firm through God's remembrance; spending brings calm only when done solely for worship, illustrated by ʿAlī's words in al-Insān 76:9.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r4.anchor: أن ثبات القلب لا يحصل إلا بذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p49/r5.claim: He also cites the report about Abū Bakr's spending as seeking only God's face, and notes the rational principle that repeating acts produces stable dispositions.

RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r1.claim: Repeated giving for God's pleasure creates a lasting disposition: even an accidental lapse quickly returns the heart toward the sacred, spiritually aligning the person with angelic and holy realities.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r1.anchor: صيرورة هذا الابتغاء والطلب ملكة مستقرة في النفس

RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says تثبيت is confident assurance that God will not waste or disappoint the donors' work, unlike the hypocrite who sees giving as wasted without belief in reward.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : المراد من التثبيت أنهم ينفقونها

RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وعطاء
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ interpret تثبيت as careful placement of alms among people of integrity; al-Ḥasan says a donor gives when the motive is truly for God.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسن ومجاهد وعطاء : المراد أن المنفق

RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r4.claim: The word ربوة means elevated, swelling ground; the author favors fertile soil that rises and grows with rain over interpreters' ordinary hill, citing Q 22:5 and the contrast with sterile stone.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r4.anchor: وأصلها من قولهم : ربا الشيء يربو إذا ازداد وارتفع

RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r5.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r5.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read ربوة with fatḥa on rāʾ, a Tamīm dialect; the other readers use ḍamma, the more common Qurashī form, among seven variants.
RAZI-FULL:v7p49#2/r5.anchor: قرأ عاصم وابن عامر { بربوة } بفتح الراء

RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r1.claim: Exegetes say a garden on a hill yields better, but al-Rāzī objects that elevation or a valley each has disadvantages and prefers fertile swelling soil, supported by Q 22:5 and the stone contrast.
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r1.anchor: البستان إذا كان في ربوة من الأرض كان أحسن وأكثر ريعا

RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr lighten أكلها; the remaining readers intensify it. The word means edible fruit or produce, as in Ibrāhīm 14:25, with lexical poetry cited.
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو { أكلها } بالتخفيف

RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads ضعفين as twice as much; ʿAṭāʾ says a single year's yield equals another garden's two-year yield, while al-Aṣamm and Abū Muslim give related doubled-yield readings.
RAZI-FULL:v7p50/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : { اتت أكلها * ضعفين } يعني مثلين

RAZI-FULL:v7p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p51/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p51/r1.claim: Ṭall is light rain. Either a fertile garden preserves its full yield despite receiving only light rain, or it still yields some fruit; sincere giving is never wasted, little or much.

RAZI-FULL:v7p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p51/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p51/r2.claim: God sees the amount and manner of spending and its motives, then recompenses each person accordingly, for good with good and evil with evil.
RAZI-FULL:v7p51/r2.anchor: هو تعالى عالم بكمية النفقات وكيفيتها

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r2.claim: Rain imagery contrasts charity spoiled by bad intention with giving done for God’s pleasure and secure faith.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r2.anchor: These verses compare the merit of two kinds of giving through the symbolism of rain striking the earth

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r4.claim: Rain on a fertile garden doubles its yield, symbolizing charity given with the right intention.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r4.anchor: the garden to double its yield, symbolizing the fruit of charity with the right intention

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r5.claim: Even without a downpour, a softer rain lets the garden thrive and bear fruit.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r5.anchor: even if the amount of rain is not great, the garden will at least thrive normally and bear its fruit

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r6.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r6.claim: Some commentators say elevated oases gather rich earth and flourish; because streams do not reach them, rain alone nourishes them.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r6.anchor: Some commentators mention that certain kinds of oases flourish and have rich earth collect on them when they are slightly elevated

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r7.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r7.claim: Others read bi-rabwah as something that rises, meaning fertile soil from which crops grow upward.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r7.anchor: Others say that upon a hill (

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r8.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī argues hills lack streams and face too much wind, while hollows flood; he says level ground is best and prefers a meaning tied to growth.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r8.anchor: Al-Rāzī argues that a garden upon a hill would not be reached by streams and would be exposed to too much wind

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r9.claim: A hadith says God grows a lawfully earned date given in charity until it becomes mountain-sized or larger.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r9.anchor: When a person gives a lawfully earned date in charity, God takes it in His Hand and causes it to grow

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r10.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r10.claim: IK and Ṭ understand giving out of inner confirmation as expressing certainty of faith in the act of giving.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r10.anchor: means that the givers affirm and have certainty of faith in their act of giving (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r11.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r11.claim: Z reads inner confirmation as confirmation of God’s Truth or certainty.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r11.anchor: that they do so because they have confirmation of the Truth of God or certainty (Z)

STUDYQURAN:2:264/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r12.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r12.claim: Q and R understand the phrase as giving carefully and confirming that charity is placed where it will be used properly.
STUDYQURAN:2:264/r12.anchor: they take care and confirm where they place their charity to make sure that it is used properly (Q, R)

TAB-FULL:v4p667/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r1.claim: The parable concerns people who give wealth in obedience to God, supporting needy fighters and other acts of obedience while seeking God’s pleasure.
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r1.anchor: سبيل الله ويقوون بها أهل الحاجة من الغزاة والمجاهدين في سبيل الله وفي غير ذلك من طاعات الله طلب مرضاته

TAB-FULL:v4p667/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r2.claim: “Establishing themselves” means God confirms their resolve and strengthens their judgment to spend, because they trust and believe His promise.
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r2.anchor: وتثبيتا لهم على إنفاق ذلك في طاعة الله وتحقيقا

TAB-FULL:v4p667/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r3.speaker: ابن رواحة
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r3.claim: Ibn Rawāḥa’s verse uses tathbīt for strengthening or confirming, supporting al-Tabari’s lexical explanation.
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r3.anchor: فثبت الله ما آتاك من حسن … تثبيت موسى ونصرا كالذي نصروا

TAB-FULL:v4p667/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r4.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbi glosses “establishing themselves” as belief and certainty, and in another wording as conviction and support.
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r4.anchor: عن الشعبي: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} [البقرة: 265] قال: «تصديقا ويقينا»

TAB-FULL:v4p667/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r5.claim: Qatada says it means certainty from within; tathbīt is certainty.
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} [البقرة: 265] قال: «يقينا من أنفسهم»

TAB-FULL:v4p667/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r6.claim: Abu Salih glosses it as certainty arising from within themselves.
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r6.anchor: عن أبي صالح، في قوله: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} [البقرة: 265] يقول: «يقينا من عند أنفسهم»

TAB-FULL:v4p667/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r7.claim: Another group interprets the phrase as donors carefully checking where to place their charity.
TAB-FULL:v4p667/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى قوله: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} [البقرة: 265] أنهم كانوا يتثبتون

TAB-FULL:v4p670/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets the phrase as donors carefully choosing where to place their money.
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} [البقرة: 265] قال ": يتثبتون أين يضعون أموالهم "

TAB-FULL:v4p670/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says they deliberated where to put their alms; a sincere intention led them to proceed, while doubt made them hold back.
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r2.anchor: سمعت الحسن، قرأ: {ابتغاء مرضاة الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} قال: «كان الرجل إذا هم بصدقة تثبت، فإن كان لله مضى

TAB-FULL:v4p670/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r3.claim: Al-Tabari considers this interpretation remote from the verse’s wording: if the intended sense were donors deliberating, the verbal noun should be تثبّتا, not تثبيتا.
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r3.anchor: وهذا التأويل الذي ذكرناه عن مجاهد والحسن تأويل بعيد المعنى

TAB-FULL:v4p670/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r4.claim: The form supports God confirming the donors’ resolve and certainty; compare the distinct pattern in “devote yourself to Him completely,” where the preceding verb licenses an implied expression.
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r4.anchor: ولكن معنى ذلك ما قلنا من أنه: وتثبيت من أنفس القوم إياهم بصحة العزم واليقين بوعد الله

TAB-FULL:v4p670/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r5.claim: Arabic can use a verbal noun whose source verb differs from the preceding verb when the context makes the omitted verb clear, as in “God caused you to grow from the earth as growth.”
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r5.anchor: كما قال جل وعز: {والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا} [نوح: 17] وقال: {وأنبتها نباتا حسنا} [آل عمران: 37]

TAB-FULL:v4p670/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r6.claim: The disputed clause has no preceding verb that could license interpreting تثبيتا as a shifted verbal noun for “they deliberated,” so that reading fails grammatically.
TAB-FULL:v4p670/r6.anchor: وليس قوله: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} [البقرة: 265] كلاما يجوز أن يكون متوهما به أنه معدول عن بنائه

TAB-FULL:v4p672/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p672/r1.claim: Qatada glosses “establishing themselves” as seeking reward from themselves.
TAB-FULL:v4p672/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: {وتثبيتا من أنفسهم} [البقرة: 265] يقول: «احتسابا من أنفسهم»

TAB-FULL:v4p672/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p672/r2.claim: Al-Tabari finds “seeking reward” remote from the meaning of تثبيت; only if souls were encouraging their owners to seek reward could it indirectly explain the phrase.
TAB-FULL:v4p672/r2.anchor: وهذا القول أيضا بعيد المعنى من معنى التثبيت

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r1.claim: The garden image compares sincere, non-injurious charity given in obedience and in trust of God’s promise with a garden on a raised, elevated plot.
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r1.anchor: وتصديقا من أنفسهم بوعده، {كمثل جنة} [البقرة: 265] والجنة: البستان

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r2.claim: Janna means a garden; rabwa is ground raised above runoff, with richer soil whose gardens and crops bear better fruit.
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r2.anchor: والربوة من الأرض: ما نشز منها فارتفع عن السيل، وإنما وصفها بذلك

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r3.speaker: الأعشى
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r3.claim: Al-Aʿsha describes a verdant garden in the uplands, whose planting and growth are stronger than those of valleys and ravines.
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r3.anchor: ما روضة من رياض الحزن معشبة … خضراء جاد عليها مسبل هطل

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r4.claim: Readers use three forms of rabwa: with ḍamma, common across the Hijaz, Medina, and Iraq; with fatḥa, used by some Syrians and Kufans and attributed to Tamim; and with kasra, reported from Ibn ʿAbbas.
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r4.anchor: وفي الربوة لغات ثلاث، وقد قرأ بكل لغة منهن جماعة من القراء

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabari allows reading rabwa only with ḍamma or fatḥa and prefers ḍamma as the more widespread Arabic form; he rejects kasra.
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r5.anchor: وأنا لقراءتها بضمها أشد إيثارا مني بفتحها؛ لأنها أشهر اللغتين في العرب

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r6.claim: Rabwa is named for its rising and thickening, from rabā, “to increase or rise.”
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r6.anchor: وإنما سميت الربوة؛ لأنها ربت فغلظت وعلت، من قول القائل

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r7.claim: Mujahid calls the rabwa an open, level, elevated place.
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {كمثل جنة بربوة} [البقرة: 265] قال: " الربوة: المكان الظاهر المستوي "

TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r8.claim: Qatada describes the rabwa as a rise in the land.
TAB-FULL:v4p672#2/r8.anchor: عن قتادة: {كمثل جنة بربوة} [البقرة: 265] يقول: «بنشز من الأرض»

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak defines rabwa as high ground without rivers, where gardens grow.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك: {كمثل جنة بربوة} [البقرة: 265] " والربوة: المكان المرتفع الذي لا تجري فيه الأنهار

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r2.claim: Al-Suddi calls rabwa a raised portion of land.

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r3.claim: Al-Rabi glosses rabwa as a rise in the land.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r3.anchor: عن الربيع: {كمثل جنة بربوة} [البقرة: 265] «والربوة النشز من الأرض»

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says rabwa is high ground where rivers do not flow.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {كمثل جنة بربوة} [البقرة: 265] قال: «المكان المرتفع الذي لا تجري فيه الأنهار»

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r5.claim: Al-Hasan offers a different view: rabwa is level land raised above the waters.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r5.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {كمثل جنة بربوة} [البقرة: 265] قال: «هي الأرض المستوية التي تعلو فوق المياه»

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r6.claim: Wābil is intense, heavy rain; after it falls, the garden bears twice the fruit, while ṭall is dew or gentle rain.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r6.anchor: وأما قوله: {فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل} [البقرة: 265] فإن الطل: هو الندى واللين من المطر

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r7.claim: Aḳl with ḍamma means edible food or fruit, whereas akl with fatḥa and a still k means the act of eating.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r7.anchor: والأكل: هو الشيء المأكول، وهو مثل الرعب والهزء وما أشبه ذلك من الأسماء التي تأتي على فعل؛ وأما الأكل بفتح الألف وتسكين الكاف

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r8.speaker: الشاعر
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r8.claim: The cited line contrasts an eaten meal with hunger, illustrating akl as the act of eating.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r8.anchor: وما أكلة أكلتها بغنيمة … ولا جوعة إن جعتها بغرام

TAB-FULL:v4p675/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that ṭall means dew.
TAB-FULL:v4p675/r9.anchor: قال ابن جريج: {فطل} [البقرة: 265] «ندى» عن عطاء الخراساني، عن ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r1.claim: The verse describes spending in God's obedience without reminding or hurting recipients, seeking God's approval.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r1.anchor: كما ضعفت ثمرة هذه الجنة التي وصفت صفتها حين جاد الوابل فإن أخطأ هذا الوابل فالطل، كذلك يضعف الله صدقة المتصدق والمنفق ماله ابتغاء مرضاته

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses ṭall as a light shower.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: {فإن لم يصبها وابل فطل} [البقرة: 265] «أي طش»

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains ṭall as fine, gentle rain.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r4.anchor: الرذاذ من المطر، يعني اللين منه

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r5.claim: Like the orchard bears abundantly in either heavy rain or drizzle, sincere almsgiving is multiplied and never wasted, whether little or much.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r5.anchor: كذلك يضعف الله صدقة المتصدق والمنفق ماله ابتغاء مرضاته وتثبيتا من نفسه من غير من ولا أذى

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the spender's reward is doubled as the orchard's yield is doubled.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r6.anchor: كما أضعفت ثمرة تلك الجنة، فكذلك تضاعف ثمرة هذا المنفق ضعفين

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r7.claim: Qatāda says the believer's good is never lost, whether the garden receives heavy rain or drizzle.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r7.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله لعمل المؤمن، يقول: ليس لخيره خلف، كما ليس لخير هذه الجنة خلف

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the orchard is a parable for one who spends seeking God's pleasure.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r8.anchor: هذا مثل من أنفق ماله ابتغاء مرضاة الله

TAB-FULL:v4p677/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r9.claim: The conditional implies kāna: the meaning is that if heavy rain did not strike, drizzle did; the verb is understood in the past construction.
TAB-FULL:v4p677/r9.anchor: فآتت أكلها ضعفين، فإن لم يكن الوابل أصابها، أصابها طل، وذلك في الكلام نحو قول القائل

TAB-FULL:v4p678/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p678/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p678/r1.claim: The cited poetic line illustrates the omitted verb in the conditional construction.
TAB-FULL:v4p678/r1.anchor: إذا ما انتسبنا لم تلدني لئيمة … ولم تجدي من أن تقري بها بدا

TAB-FULL:v4p679/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p679/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p679/r1.claim: God sees all spending and other deeds, distinguishes ostentatious or hurtful giving from sincere giving, records them, and repays each person accordingly.
TAB-FULL:v4p679/r1.anchor: فيحصي عليكم حتى يجازي جميعكم جزاءه على عمله، إن خيرا فخير، وإن شرا فشر

TAB-FULL:v4p679/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p679/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p679/r2.claim: The closing warning cautions against prohibited conduct and neglect of obligations because every act is seen and recorded by God.
TAB-FULL:v4p679/r2.anchor: التحذير من عقابه في النفقات التي ينفقها عباده، وغير ذلك من الأعمال أن يأتي أحد من خلقه ما قد تقدم فيه بالنهي عنه

TABATABAI:2:261-274/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r1.claim: The connected themes suggest this passage was revealed as one unit: spending grows seven hundredfold or more, sincere giving bears fruit, ostentation and reminders or harm ruin reward, good wealth should be given, the poor detained in God's path are recipients, and the reward is great.

TABATABAI:2:261-274/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r2.claim: The passage orders its teaching around purpose (giving for God, not people), manner (without reproach or injury), quality (good rather than bad wealth), recipient (the needy constrained in God's path), and reward.
TABATABAI:2:261-274/r2.anchor: وهو أن يكون لله لا للناس

TABATABAI:2:265/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:265/r1.claim: Seeking God's pleasure means intending His face: for the commanded servant, God's 'face' is His satisfaction with obedience after the command first addresses the servant.
TABATABAI:2:265/r1.anchor: فابتغاء مرضاة الله هو إرادة وجهه عز وجل

TABATABAI:2:265/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:265/r2.claim: One reported interpretation takes 'stabilizing themselves' to mean assent and certainty.

TABATABAI:2:265/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:265/r3.claim: Another reported interpretation says they carefully decide where to place their money.
TABATABAI:2:265/r3.anchor: وقيل هو التثبت أي يتثبتون أين يضعون أموالهم

TABATABAI:2:265/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:265/r4.claim: A further interpretation says they verify their spending, proceeding if it is for God and withholding if ostentation intrudes.
TABATABAI:2:265/r4.anchor: وقيل هو التثبت في الانفاق، فإن كان لله أمضى

TABATABAI:2:265/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:265/r5.claim: Another interpretation makes it a resolve of the self to obey God.
TABATABAI:2:265/r5.anchor: وقيل التثبيت توطين النفس على طاعة الله تعالى

TABATABAI:2:265/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:2:265/r6.claim: Another interpretation is to establish oneself in faith by habituating oneself to give for God's sake.
TABATABAI:2:265/r6.anchor: وقيل هو تمكين النفس في منازل الإيمان بتعويدها على بذل المال

TABATABAI:2:265/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:265/r7.claim: The author says none of these reported explanations fits the wording without strained interpretation.
TABATABAI:2:265/r7.anchor: بأن شيئا من الأقوال لا ينطبق على الآية إلا بتكلف

TABATABAI:2:265/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:265/r8.claim: The passage first excludes ostentation, which invalidates a deed from the outset, and spending later spoiled by mann or harm; it then describes sincere givers who hold fast to their pure intention.
TABATABAI:2:265/r8.anchor: وهم الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء وجه الله ثم يقرون أنفسهم على الثبات

TABATABAI:2:265-266/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r1.claim: Tathbīt is the self's resolve to keep itself firm in the pure intention it formed; min marks its source, anfus is the agent, and the implied object is the self itself.
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r1.anchor: والتقدير تثبيتا من أنفسهم لأنفسهم، أو مفعول مطلق لفعل من مادته

TABATABAI:2:265-266/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r2.claim: Rabwa derives from growth and means good elevated land; akl is what is eaten, and tall is weak rain with little effect.
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r2.anchor: والربوة بالحركات الثلاث في الراء الأرض الجيدة التي تزيد وتعلو

TABATABAI:2:265-266/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r3.claim: The garden parable says sincere spending unfailingly bears good fruit because divine care remains attached to it, though yield varies with the purity of intention and the quality of the rain.
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r3.anchor: فإن العناية الإلهية واقعة عليه متعلقة به لانحفاظ اتصاله بالله سبحانه

TABATABAI:2:265-266/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r4.claim: God's seeing means He distinguishes differing deeds and rewards without confusing one person's reward with another's.
TABATABAI:2:265-266/r4.anchor: ولا يختلط عليه ثواب الأعمال المختلفة فيعطي ثواب هذا لذاك

TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r6.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r6.claim: Al-Qummī glosses ṣafwān as a large rock, wābil as rain, tall as nighttime dew on plants, and iʿṣār as winds.
TABATABAI:2:261-274#7/r6.anchor: والصفوان هي الصخرة الكبيرة التي تكون في المفازة

TABRISI:2:265/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265/r1.claim: Asim and Ibn Amir read ربوة with fatḥa, most others with ḍamma, and Ibn Abbas has a rare kasra; Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr lighten أكلها while others double it.
TABRISI:2:265/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم وابن عامر بربوة بفتح الراء والباقون بضمها

TABRISI:2:265/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265/r2.claim: The author chooses the ḍamma form of ربوة, meaning a raised hill; أكل means produce or food rather than the act of eating, as 14:25 shows.

TABRISI:2:265/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265/r3.claim: A thing's double can mean itself plus an equal, while its two doubles mean two equal amounts added; some use double to mean two times the original.

TABRISI:2:265/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265/r4.claim: طل is light rain; the word also names blood left unavenged, a ruin's standing outline, or animal fat, all related to the image of dew or rain.
TABRISI:2:265/r4.anchor: والطل المطر الصغار يقال أطلت السماء فهي مطلة

TABRISI:2:265/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265/r5.claim: In syntax, seeking God's approval is a purpose, تثبيتا coordinates with it, the hill phrase modifies the garden, and the twofold produce describes its state.
TABRISI:2:265/r5.anchor: ابتغاء مرضاة الله مفعول له وتثبيتا معطوف عليه

TABRISI:2:265/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والسدي والشعبي
TABRISI:2:265/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and al-Sha'bi explain تثبيتا من أنفسهم as strong conviction and insight in religion.
TABRISI:2:265/r6.anchor: بقوة اليقين والبصيرة في الدين عن سعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:2:265/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r7.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
TABRISI:2:265/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say spenders confirm for themselves where their charity should be placed; the author answers that confirming themselves is itself a valid sense of making firm.
TABRISI:2:265/r7.anchor: وقيل معناه أنهم يثبتون أين يضعون صدقاتهم

TABRISI:2:265/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r8.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:2:265/r8.claim: Abu Ali al-Jubba'i reads تثبيتا as making oneself steadfast in obedience to God.
TABRISI:2:265/r8.anchor: وقيل معناه وتوطينا لنفوسهم على الثبوت على طاعة الله

TABRISI:2:265/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265/r9.claim: A garden on high ground yields better and more than land receiving pooled runoff.
TABRISI:2:265/r9.anchor: لأن نبتها يكون أحسن وريعها أكثر من المستغل

TABRISI:2:265#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265#2/r1.claim: Heavy rain gives the high garden twice the crop it would produce on ordinary lowland; the doubled yield may also mean two harvests yearly, six months apart.
TABRISI:2:265#2/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معناه مرتين في كل سنة واحدة

TABRISI:2:265#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:2:265#2/r2.claim: Abu Abd Allah explains the doubled produce as the multiplication of reward for spending to seek God's approval.
TABRISI:2:265#2/r2.anchor: معناه يتضاعف أجر من أنفق ماله مرضاة الله

TABRISI:2:265#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265#2/r3.claim: Even if heavy rain does not reach it, the garden receives light rain and remains fruitful; its benefit is reliable in either case.
TABRISI:2:265#2/r3.anchor: أراد به أن خيرها لا يخلف على كل حال

TABRISI:2:265#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:265#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:265#2/r4.claim: God sees what people do and rewards them accordingly; alternatively, he knows who acts ostentatiously and who sincerely, a warning and encouragement.
TABRISI:2:265#2/r4.anchor: وقيل عالم بالمرائي والمخلص وفيه ترغيب وترهيب

THALABI:v2p263#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p263#2/r1.claim: Seeking God's pleasure means desiring His approval; “stabilizing themselves” has several interpretations reported below.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r1.anchor: ابتغاء مرضات الله طلب رضا الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم

THALABI:v2p263#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي والكلبي والضحاك
THALABI:v2p263#2/r2.claim: Al-Jalabī, al-Kalbī, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk take tathbīt as affirmation: donors give zakat willingly, knowing what they spend is better for them than what they keep.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r2.anchor: قال الشعبي والكلبي والضحاك: يعني تصديقا من أنفسهم يخرجون الزكاة طيبة بها أنفسهم

THALABI:v2p263#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r3.speaker: السدي وأبو صالح وأبو روق وابن زيد والمفضل
THALABI:v2p263#2/r3.claim: These authorities explain tathbīt as certainty that God will replace what they spend.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r3.anchor: السدي وأبو صالح وأبو روق وابن زيد والمفضل: على يقين إخلاف الله عليهم.

THALABI:v2p263#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v2p263#2/r4.claim: Qatāda explains it as seeking reward in faith.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r4.anchor: قتادة: احتسابا بإيمان من أنفسهم، عطاء ومجاهد:

THALABI:v2p263#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r5.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
THALABI:v2p263#2/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid say the donors are assured they will not lose their wealth; Mujāhid's reading says “for their own selves.”
THALABI:v2p263#2/r5.anchor: عطاء ومجاهد: مثبتون أي لا يضيعون أموالهم، وكذلك قرأ مجاهد:

THALABI:v2p263#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
