THALABI:v2p263#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a person considering charity deliberates: if it is for God, he gives, but if another motive is mixed in, he holds back; tathbīt here means deliberation.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن: كان الرجل إذا هم بصدقة تثبت إن كان لله أعطى

THALABI:v2p263#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك
THALABI:v2p263#2/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Abū Mālik interpret the phrase as lessening their sin.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r7.anchor: سعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك: تخفيفا في ذنبهم.

THALABI:v2p263#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r8.speaker: ابن كيسان
THALABI:v2p263#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kaysān reads the phrase as sincerity and habituating themselves to obey God in their spending.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r8.anchor: ابن كيسان: إخلاصا وتوطينا لأنفسهم على طاعة الله عز وجل في نفقاتهم،

THALABI:v2p263#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v2p263#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj says they spend while acknowledging that God watches them.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r9.anchor: الزجاج: ينفقونها مقرين بأن الله عز وجل رقيب عليهم.

THALABI:v2p263#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p263#2/r10.claim: The root of tathbīt is to make something firm: the expression describes someone who verifies an undertaking, persists in it, and strengthens himself to do it; a poem illustrates the word.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r10.anchor: وأصل هذه الكلمة من قول السائل: ثبت فلان في هذا الأمر إذا حققه

THALABI:v2p263#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v2p263#2/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says a garden with date palms is called jannah, whereas a vineyard is called firdaws.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r11.anchor: قال الفراء: إذا كان في البستان نخل فهو جنة، وإذا كان كرم فهو فردوس.

THALABI:v2p263#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p263#2/r12.claim: Mujāhid is cited for reading the comparison as like a seed, and the segment begins reporting regional readings of rabwah.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r12.anchor: وقول مجاهد: كمثل حبة بالحاء والباء بربوة

THALABI:v2p263#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p263#2/r13.speaker: السليمي والعطاردي والحسن وعاصم وابن عامر
THALABI:v2p263#2/r13.claim: These readers pronounce rabwah with fatḥa on the rāʾ in this verse and in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn; the source calls it the Banū Tamīm dialect.
THALABI:v2p263#2/r13.anchor: قرأ السليمي والعطاردي والحسن وعاصم وابن عامر: بربوة بفتح الراء هاهنا

THALABI:v2p264/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن كثير والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وأيوب
THALABI:v2p264/r1.claim: These readers pronounce rabwah with ḍamma on rāʾ in both places; Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd prefer it as the fullest and best-known language.
THALABI:v2p264/r1.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن كثير والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي

THALABI:v2p264/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r2.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
THALABI:v2p264/r2.claim: Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī reads rabāwah with an added alif and kasra on rāʾ; all readings mean level elevated land with flowing water.
THALABI:v2p264/r2.anchor: وقرأ أشهب العقيلي: برباوة بالألف وكسر الراء فيها.

THALABI:v2p264/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p264/r3.claim: The raised ground is called rabwah because it rises and grows; plants flourish there, and its land is level and supplied with water.
THALABI:v2p264/r3.anchor: وهي جميعا المكان المرتفع المستوي الذي تجري فيه الأنهار

THALABI:v2p264/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r4.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
THALABI:v2p264/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr read akulahā with a light kāf; the other readers double it, and the word means fruit.
THALABI:v2p264/r4.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو: أكلها بالتخفيف والباقون بالتشديد

THALABI:v2p264/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r5.speaker: المفضل
THALABI:v2p264/r5.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal defines akl as the abundance and quality of what strengthens something, like a garment containing much yarn; here the garden gives double fruit.
THALABI:v2p264/r5.anchor: قال المفضل: الأكل: كثرة ما في الشيء مما يجود ويقوى به

THALABI:v2p264/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r6.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v2p264/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the garden produced in one year what another garden produced in two.
THALABI:v2p264/r6.anchor: قال عطاء: حملت في سنة من الريع ما تحمل غيرها في سنتين.

THALABI:v2p264/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r7.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v2p264/r7.claim: ʿIkrimah says the garden yielded twice in one year.
THALABI:v2p264/r7.anchor: قال عكرمة: حملت في السنة مرتين.

THALABI:v2p264/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p264/r8.claim: Ṭall means light, gentle rain; al-Suddī identifies it as dew.
THALABI:v2p264/r8.anchor: فطل أي فطش وهو أضعف المطر وألينه

THALABI:v2p264/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p264/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v2p264/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says the comparison is Egyptian land, which grows well without rain but weakens when rain falls; likewise sincere charity earns multiplied reward whether small or large, without reproach or harm.
THALABI:v2p264/r9.anchor: وهذا مثل ضربه الله عز وجل لعمل المؤمن المخلص

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r1.claim: This is a parable for those who spend seeking God's approval without reminding recipients of the gift or hurting them; the syntax omits “spending,” as in “God's horses, ride.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r1.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله عز وجل لمن ينفق، يريد ما عند الله ولا يمن ولا يؤذي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r2.claim: He reads تثبيتا as spending with certainty that God will reward it; the sincere are sure of that recompense, unlike hypocrites who give for show without expecting reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r2.anchor: أي: وينفقونها مقرين بأنها مما يثيب الله عليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r4.speaker: الشعبي والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r4.claim: They interpret it as affirmation or sincere belief that what they spend benefits them more than what they keep.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r4.anchor: يعني: تصديقا من أنفسهم، يعلمون أن ما أخرجوا خير لهم مما تركوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r5.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r5.claim: They take تثبيتا as deliberation: carefully selecting a pious, upright recipient for charity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r5.anchor: يتثبت في صدقته، فيضعها في أهل الصلاح والعفاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r6.claim: He says a person considering charity should test the motive: proceed if it is for God, but hold back if doubt is mixed into it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r6.anchor: فإن كان لله أمضى، وإن خالطه شك أمسك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r7.claim: The deliberation sense works because they steady themselves in seeking recipients and directing funds properly; Arabic similarly says one who restrains himself is restrained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p415/r7.anchor: لأنهم ثبتوا أنفسهم تثبيتا في طلب المستحق، وصرف المال في وجهه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r1.claim: Rabwa means elevated ground and has several dialectal forms; al-Akhfash prefers the ḍamma form because its plural is usually الربى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r2.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r2.claim: He prefers ربوة with ḍamma; it comes from rising or increasing, like الرابية, and is related to swelling breath and financial الربا.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r2.anchor: قال الأخفش والذي نختاره: ربوة بالضم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r3.claim: An orchard on high ground yields more and grows greener when it has enough water; the Aʿsha's poem names the fertile gardens of al-Ḥazn as an example.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p416/r3.anchor: لأن الموضع المرتفع من الأرض إذا كان له ما يرويه من الماء فهو أكثر ريعا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r1.claim: Wābil is the strongest rain; akl means edible food or fruit, as in 14:25, and lexically can mean a person's worldly share, with variant vowel and plural forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أصابها وابل} وهو أشد المطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r2.claim: They take the crop in this verse to mean fruit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: الأكل: المراد به الثمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r3.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r3.claim: The orchard produces in one year twice the crop another orchard produces in two years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r3.anchor: يريد: حملت في سنة من الريع ما يحمل غيرها في سنتين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r4.claim: Ṭall is a gentle rain with small drops; the source gives related verb and adjective forms and a customary prayer for abundant rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r4.anchor: وهو المطر اللين الصغار القطر، يقال: طلت السماء تطل طلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r5.claim: The conditional “if no heavy rain reaches it, then dew” has an omitted “if it receives dew,” as in the example about freeing two or one slave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r5.anchor: فيه إضمار المعنى: فإن يكن لم يصبها وابل فطل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r6.claim: Whether the orchard receives heavy rain or dew, its yield remains abundant; likewise God multiplies the sincere believer's reward whether the charity is small or great.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p418/r6.anchor: ثواب صدقة المؤمن المخلص، سواء قلت نفقته وصدقت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r1.claim: The sincere spender seeks God's pleasure and has inward conviction and belief in the reward, unlike a hypocrite.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r1.anchor: من أنفسهم } بالثواب لا كالمنافق الذي لا يؤمن بالثواب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r2.claim: A garden on elevated ground yields more than one on low ground, and heavy rain makes it produce double its usual crop.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r3.claim: Even light rain leaves the elevated garden fruitful and blessed; likewise God multiplies a believer's reward whether the gift is small or large.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r3.anchor: كذلك يضعف الله ثواب صدقة المؤمن قلت نفقته أم كثرت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r4.claim: A heavy downpour produces a crop twice that of other gardens' two-year yield.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r4.anchor: حملت في سنة من الريع ما يحمل غيرها في سنتين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r5.claim: The garden simile leads into the example of the ostentatious spender and the person who neglects obedience until death.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:265/r5.anchor: ثم قرر مثل المرائي في النفقة والمفرط في الطاعة إلى أن يموت

ELMALILI:2:265/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:265/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:265/r1.claim: The sincere donor seeks God's pleasure and uses wealth to steady themselves, their deeds, and their companions against corrupt inclinations and instability, making good works a settled habit.
ELMALILI:2:265/r1.anchor: hayr ü hasenâtı kendilerine meleke-i sâbite kılmak ve ondan sonra her nevi fezâil ve ibâdâtı suhûletle yapmak

ELMALILI:2:265/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:265/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:265/r2.claim: A garden on a high hill yields twice its usual fruit under a heavy rain; the earlier rain that stripped rock becomes mercy here.
ELMALILI:2:265/r2.anchor: O kayayı cascavlak bırakan yağmur, bu tepede ‘ayn-ı rahmet olur

ELMALILI:2:265/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:265/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:265/r3.claim: The garden's doubled yield does not reduce the earlier promise of seven hundredfold; it adds another multiplication.
ELMALILI:2:265/r3.anchor: Bu temsil bâlâdaki bire yedi yüz ve daha kat kat vaadini tenzil etmiş değil, belki bir daha katlamıştır

ELMALILI:2:265/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:265/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:265/r4.claim: Even without a heavy downpour, a light drizzle or slight moisture is enough for the garden to produce its yield.
ELMALILI:2:265/r4.anchor: hafif bir yağmur, az bir nem de yetişir, vereceğini yine verir

ELMALILI:2:265/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:265/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:265/r5.claim: Because God sees and knows deeds, donors must avoid showing off and remain sincere in private and public.
ELMALILI:2:265/r5.anchor: Sakın gösteriş yapmayın, gizlide âşikârda ihlâstan ayrılmayın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:265/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:265/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:265/r1.claim: Giving to those in need from faith and sincere inner conviction for God's pleasure yields in proportion to intention, like an orchard protected from harmful winds that bears much in heavy rain and some in drizzle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:265/r1.anchor: Allah rızâsı için ve içlerinden gelerek, gönüllerindeki inancın yönlendirdiği bir karara dayanarak muhtaçlara yardım edenler, bu niyet, şuur ve samimiyetin derecesine göre sonuç alacaklardır

FARRA:v1p489/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p489/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p489/r3.claim: The heading notes an analysis of an elided kāna in the conditional phrase about the garden receiving no heavy rain.
FARRA:v1p489/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى: «فإن لم يصبها وابل» وقوله: «إلا أن تغمضوا فيه» والكلام على إضمار كان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r4.claim: He glosses تثبيتا من أنفسهم as confirmation made real from within themselves.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r5.claim: A garden on an elevated place is especially fruitful, since gardens and orchards are at their best on heights.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r5.anchor: وأحسن ما تكون الجنان والرياض: على الربا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r6.claim: وابل means the heaviest rain, which makes the garden yield twice its usual produce.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r6.anchor: أصابها وابل وهو: أشد المطر، فأضعفت في الحمل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r7.claim: طل is lighter rain; even with it the garden’s fruit yield is not diminished from what it would be with heavy rain.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p195#2/r7.anchor: وهو: أضعف المطر. فتلك حالها في النزل وتضاعف الثمر

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r1.speaker: طه حسين
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r1.claim: Ṭāhā Ḥusayn argues that the names of two figures appearing in both Torah and Qur'an do not by themselves establish their historical existence.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r1.anchor: ورود هذين الاسمين فى التوراة والقرآن لا يكفى لإثبات وجودهما التاريخى

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r2.speaker: الشيخ محمد عبده
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r2.claim: Muḥammad ʿAbduh says Qur'anic stories aim at admonition and reflection, not historical documentation or belief in every detail; their wording and structure signal moral approval and censure.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r2.anchor: وقبل طه حسين تحدث الشيخ محمد عبده عن أغراض القصص القرآنى فقال

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r3.speaker: محمد عبده
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r3.claim: In al-Manār, ʿAbduh's view is quoted that prophetic stories are lessons and reminders, not histories of peoples, cities, or exact events.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r3.anchor: جميع قصص الرسل فيه عبرة وتذكرة لا تاريخ شعوب ومدائن ولا تحقيق وقائع ومواقع

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r4.speaker: محمد عبده
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r4.claim: A second al-Manār passage says Qur'anic stories present signs and lessons within encounters between messengers and their peoples, to warn opponents and strengthen the Prophet and believers; they do not give full chronology or detail.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r4.anchor: ولذلك لم تُذْكَر قصةٌ بترتيبِها وتفاصيلها وإنما يذكر موضع العبرة فيها

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r5.speaker: خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r5.claim: In reply to criticism, Khalaf Allāh said his theory of Qur'anic stories followed the method of later interpreters and the position of the Imam, Muḥammad ʿAbduh.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r5.anchor: هذه هى نظريتى فى القصص وهى نظرية تعتمد على طريقة الخلف ومذهب الأستاذ الإمام

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r6.speaker: كتاب
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r6.claim: Several writers rejected Khalaf Allāh's attribution to Muḥammad ʿAbduh and Rashīd Riḍā, accusing him of ignorance and misunderstanding.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r6.anchor: لم يقبل عدة كتاب ما نسبه خلف الله لمحمد عبده ورشيد رضا، واتهموه بالجهل وسوء الفهم

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r7.speaker: محمد إقبال
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r7.claim: Muḥammad Iqbāl reads Adam's descent as a symbol of humanity's rise from instinctive desire to awareness of a free self able to doubt and disobey, not as the first human's arrival on earth.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r7.anchor: وفات خلف الله أن يذكر موقف محمد إقبال الذى يرى

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r8.speaker: خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r8.claim: Khalaf Allāh calls for reading scripture's stories through a concept of the religious language in which they are expressed.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r8.anchor: يدعو خلف الله إلى إعادة النظر فى التعاطى مع لغة القرآن

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r9.speaker: خلف الله
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r9.claim: For Khalaf Allāh, sacred stories are not historical reports; their symbolic meaning is guidance, like the purpose of parables.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r9.anchor: القصص فى الكتب المقدسة لا ترد بوصفها تقريرا لحوادث تاريخية. لغة الكتاب المقدس غرضها المعنى الذى ترمز إليه القصة وهو الهداية

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r10.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r10.claim: Al-Fann al-Qaṣaṣī fī al-Qurʾān was a pioneering application of a different religious-language theory, but the approach remains largely unacceptable.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r10.anchor: كان كتاب «الفن القصصي في القرآن الكريم» منعطفًا رائدًا في تطبيق مفهوم مختلف للغة الدين

RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r11.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r11.claim: The author says contemporary Qur'anic studies remain captive to inherited Qur'anic sciences and tafsir rules, shaped by older worldviews, rather than modern perspectives and current human and social sciences, as al-Khūlī urged.
RIFAI-KHULI:c7/r11.anchor: أكثر الدراسات القرآنية أسيرة علوم القرآن وقواعد التفسير التى أنتجها المفسرون فى الماضى، ومفهومهم للغة الدين

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r1.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r1.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r1.claim: The author places Amīn al-Khūlī’s renewal in the modern Arab intellectual path led earlier by Muḥammad ʿAbduh, who attacked stagnation and championed religion’s alliance with reason.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r1.anchor: يتقدمهم بجدارة الشيخ محمد عبده (١٨٤٩–١٩٠٥) الأستاذ الإمام، إمام المجددين، وقائد جيش الهجوم على التقليد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r2.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r2.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r2.claim: ʿAbduh says over a third, even half, of the Qur’an urges reflection on cosmic signs; it prompts moral lesson, gratitude, and thought rather than prescribing natural laws or one cosmology.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r2.anchor: يقول الأستاذ الإمام: «لو أردت سرد جميع الآيات التي تدعو إلى النظر في آيات الكون، لأتيت بأكثر من ثلث القرآن

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r3.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r3.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r3.claim: ʿAbduh makes rational inquiry the first principle for acquiring faith and gives reason priority over scripture’s apparent sense in conflict; free thought is a duty of rational beings.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r3.anchor: الأصل الأول من أصول الإسلام عند محمد عبده هو النظر العقلي لتحصيل الإيمان، والأصل الثاني هو تقديم العقل على ظاهر الشرع عند التعارض بينهما

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r4.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r4.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r4.claim: ʿAbduh regards religious feeling as innate but compatible with religion’s development alongside humanity; he calls for continual rebuilding of beliefs to fit changing realities and progress in science.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r4.anchor: والنتيجة الطبيعية المنطقية لهذا أن ينتقل محمد عبده إلى تأكيد ضرورة التجديد، ورفض الجمود والتقليد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r5.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r5.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r5.claim: Changing times bring cases absent from old fiqh books; society cannot be halted for them, and stagnation alienates ordinary people when religion cannot address their lives.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r5.anchor: كان محمد عبده يقول إن الناس تحدث لهم باختلاف الزمان أمور ووقائع لم يرد لها ذكر في كتب الفقه القديمة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r6.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r6.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r6.claim: People should learn from earlier generations but scrutinize inherited traditions, keeping what accords with reason and rejecting the rest; free inquiry and critical judgment distinguish humans.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r6.anchor: هذا البحث الحر، وهذه الحاسة الناقدة فيما يرى محمد عبده، هي ما يميز الحيوان الناطق عن سائر الحيوان

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r7.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r7.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r7.claim: Al-Khūlī’s maxim says earlier generations were people of their time and later generations are people of theirs: learn from predecessors without copying them exactly.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r7.anchor: هم رجال ونحن رجال، لهم عصرهم ولنا عصرنا، نتعلم منهم ولا نحذو حذوهم النعل بالنعل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r8.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r8.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r8.claim: The author contrasts al-Khūlī, who deems the anti-renewal imitator sinful, with ʿAbduh, who went further and called the imitator an unbeliever for repeating without certainty.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r8.anchor: وإذا كان أمين الخولي يؤثم المقلد الرافض للتجديد، فإن الأمر قد سبق أن بلغ بمحمد عبده حد اعتبار المقلد كافرًا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r9.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r9.speaker: محمد عبده
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r9.claim: ʿAbduh lists imitation’s harms to language, government, society, law, religious doctrine, and education, and argues that stagnation is removable and not properly attributed to Islam.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c1/r9.anchor: أسهب عبده في التعبير عن ضيقه من التقليد والجمود على القديم، وراح في تعداد مفاسد هذا الجمود ونتائجه

NASHR:v2p133/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p133/r1.speaker: ابن جبارة
NASHR:v2p133/r1.claim: Ibn Jabbāra attributes stopping with hāʾ at ذات الشوكة, ذات لهب, and بذات الصدور to Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb; the author rejects this as contrary to the written form and performance practice.
NASHR:v2p133/r1.anchor: وزعم ابن جبارة أن ابن كثير وأبا عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب، يقفون على ذات الشوكة

NASHR:v2p133/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p133/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p133/r2.claim: At pause, an indefinite nonfeminine accusative with tanwīn is replaced by alif, as in the cited examples.
NASHR:v2p133/r2.anchor: المنصوب لمنون غير المؤنث يبدل في الوقف ألفا مطلقا كما تقدم

NASHR:v2p133/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p133/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p133/r3.claim: A singular feminine noun not written with open tāʾ has tāʾ pronounced as hāʾ at pause, whether or not it has tanwīn; جنة بربوة is an example.
NASHR:v2p133/r3.anchor: الاسم المفرد المؤنث ما لم يرسم بالتاء تبدل تاؤه وصلا هاء وقفا

NASHR:v2p459/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p459/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p459/r1.claim: An account has a caller tell Abū Sulaymān that what afflicted one hand had been placed in it, prompting him to vow to pray only with both hands extended in any weather.
NASHR:v2p459/r1.anchor: فهتف بي هاتف يا أبا سليمان قد وضعنا في هذه ما أصابها

NASHR:v2p459/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p459/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v2p459/r2.claim: When people complained of drought, the Prophet told them to kneel and call, “Lord, Lord”; they did so and received rain. Abū ʿAwāna included the report in his Ṣaḥīḥ.
NASHR:v2p459/r2.anchor: أن قوما شكوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قحوط المطر

NASHR:v2p459/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p459/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p459/r3.claim: The report that the Prophet stood to supplicate when completing the Qurʾan, cited by Ibn al-Jawzī and others, is unsound.
NASHR:v2p459/r3.anchor: وأما ما روي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان إذا ختم القرآن دعا قائما كما أورده ابن الجوزي

NASHR:v2p459/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p459/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v2p459/r5.claim: In a prayer reported by Muslim, the Prophet confesses his sin, asks forgiveness, and asks God to guide him to the best character and turn away its evil.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the Qur'an descended all at once to the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then came down over twenty years; Ibn Kathir grades the chain authentic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس قال: أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة إلى السماء الدنيا في ليلة القدر، ثم نزل بعد ذلك في عشرين سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet's ten years in Medina are undisputed; the well-known account gives thirteen years in Mecca, from age forty to sixty-three.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r2.anchor: أما إقامته بالمدينة عشرا فهذا ما لا خلاف فيه، وأما إقامته بمكة بعد النبوة فالمشهور ثلاث عشرة سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r3.claim: He offers two possible reconciliations for the shorter reckoning: omitted fractional years for brevity, or counting the period of Gabriel's companionship.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أنه حذف ما زاد على العشرة اختصارا في الكلام؛ لأن العرب كثيرا ما يحذفون الكسور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r4.speaker: أحمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir adds that Ahmad reported Mika'il was paired with the Prophet at first, conveying words or something, before Gabriel was paired with him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r4.anchor: قد روى الإمام أحمد أنه قرن به، عليه السلام، ميكائيل في ابتداء الأمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r5.claim: The report suits a book on Qur'anic virtues because revelation began in the sacred city and sacred month, combining the honor of place and time.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r5.anchor: ووجه مناسبة هذا الحديث بفضائل القرآن: أنه ابتدئ بنزوله في مكان شريف، وهو البلد الحرام، كما أنه كان في زمن شريف وهو شهر رمضان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r6.claim: Because revelation began in Ramadan, Ibn Kathir says it is recommended to increase Qur'an recitation then; Gabriel reviewed it with the Prophet yearly, twice in the year he died, for confirmation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r6.anchor: ولهذا يستحب إكثار تلاوة القرآن في شهر رمضان؛ لأنه ابتدئ نزوله فيه؛ ولهذا كان جبريل يعارض به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كل سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r7.claim: Meccan means revealed before the Hijra; Medinan means revealed after it, wherever the revelation occurred, including Mecca or ʿArafat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r7.anchor: فالمكي: ما نزل قبل الهجرة، والمدني: ما نزل بعد الهجرة، سواء كان بالمدينة أو بغيرها من أي البلاد كان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir says scholars agree on some Meccan and Medinan surahs but disagree about others; proposed systems of criteria are difficult to apply and open to objection.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r8.anchor: وقد أجمعوا على سور أنها من المكي وأخر أنها من المدني، واختلفوا في أخر، وأراد بعضهم ضبط ذلك بضوابط في تقييدها عسر ونظر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r9.claim: One proposed rule makes surahs beginning with disjoint letters Meccan except al-Baqara and Al ʿImran, and surahs addressing believers Medinan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم: كل سورة في أولها شيء من الحروف المقطعة فهي مكية إلا البقرة وآل عمران

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r10.claim: Surahs addressing people are usually Meccan but may be Medinan; Ibn Kathir gives two al-Baqara examples of the latter address.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17#2/r10.anchor: وما فيها: {ياأيها الناس} فيحتمل أن يكون من هذا ومن هذا، والغالب أنه مكي

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r1.claim: After the show-off’s charity and its reminder or harm, the passage gives the contrasting example of a believer whose charity fulfills what is commanded.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r1.anchor: لما تقدم المثل بصدقة المرائي وإتباعه بالمن والأذى أتبعه بصدقة المؤمن

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r2.claim: The spenders put their wealth into works of goodness.

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r3.anchor: ابتغاء مرضاة الله أي طلب رضا الله

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Zayd, al-Suddī, Ibn Ṣāliḥ, and Abū Muslim explain it as firmness grounded in certainty and insight.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r4.anchor: قيل: تثبيتا من أنفسهم بقوة اليقين والبصيرة، عن سعيد بن جبير والشعبي وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r5.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid explain it as carefully choosing the proper recipients for charity, paraphrased as making themselves firm in the choice.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r5.anchor: وقيل: يتثبتون. في موضع صدقاتهم، عن الحسن ومجاهد، وعلى هذا تقديره ثبتوا أنفسهم

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r6.claim: Al-Aṣamm and Abū ʿAlī explain it as preparing themselves to remain firm in obedience to their Lord.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r6.anchor: وقيل: توطينا لأنفسهم على الثبوت على طاعة ربهم، عن الأصم وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r7.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r7.claim: Qatāda glosses the phrase as seeking reward for the deed.

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r8.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r8.claim: The Qāḍī explains it as committing themselves to preserve the charity from anything that would corrupt it.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r8.anchor: وقيل: يوطنون أنفسهم على حفظها، وترك ما يفسدها، عن القاضي

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r9.claim: A janna is a garden; a rabwa is a high, level place where streams run without flooding it, a location singled out for its greater growth and yield.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r9.anchor: كمثل جنة أي بستان بربوة أي بمكان مرتفع مستو تجري فيه الأنهار فلا يعلوه الماء

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and al-Rabīʿ gloss rabwa as elevated ground.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r10.anchor: وقيل: الربوة المرتفع من الأرض، عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك ومجاهد والسدي والربيع

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r12.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r12.claim: The fruit is what grows there and is eaten; ḍiʿfayn means twofold, with al-Zajjāj explaining ḍiʿf as the original amount plus an addition.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r12.anchor: (فآتت أكلها) يعني ما نبت فيها مما يؤكل (ضعفين) يعني مثلين، عن الزجاج؛ لأن ضعف الشيء مثله زائدا عليه

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r13.speaker: عطاء
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r13.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says one year’s yield from the rabʿ is what another garden yields in two years.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r13.anchor: قال عطاء: حملت في سنة من الربع ما تحمل غيرها في سنتين

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r14.speaker: عكرمة
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r14.claim: ʿIkrima says the garden produces twice in one year.

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r15.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r15.claim: Al-Aṣamm and Abū ʿAlī take the yield as double what other gardens produce.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r15.anchor: وقال الأصم وأبو علي: ضعف ما يكون في غيره

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r16.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r16.claim: Abū Muslim explains the yield as twice the garden’s customary produce.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r16.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: مثلي ما يعهد منه

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r17.claim: The clause is elliptic: if heavy rain did not fall on it, then light rain did; the past-tense construction is explained by an omitted kāna, as in the cited manumission example.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r17.anchor: ونظيره أعتقت عبدين، فإن لم أعتق اثنين فواحدا، معناه إن لم أكن أعتق

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r18.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r18.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Rabīʿ, and Qatāda take ṭall as gentle rain; al-Suddī says it is dew.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r18.anchor: فطل: مطر لين، عن الحسن والضحاك والربيع وقتادة، وقيل: هو الندى، عن السدي

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r19.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r19.claim: The garden illustrates the believer’s deeds: it yields whether rain is light or heavy, just as God multiplies the reward for charity whether the gift is small or large and never withholds recompense; al-Ḥasan and Qatāda are cited.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r19.anchor: وهذا مثل لعمل المؤمن يعني كما أن الجنة تريع في كل حال ولا يخيب صاحبها قل المطر أو كثر

JISHUMI:v2p1032/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r20.claim: God knows people’s spending and intentions and rewards each according to what they did; Abū Muslim says He knows who is ostentatious and who is sincere.
JISHUMI:v2p1032/r20.anchor: والله بما تعملون بصير أي عالم بنفقاتكم ونياتكم يجازي كلا بحسب ما عمل

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r1.speaker: عاصم
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read rabwa with fatḥa on rāʾ, also used in 23:50; the other readers use ḍamma, the more common Qurashī form. Ibn ʿAbbās is reported with kasra, and another report has ribāwa with kasra and alif.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r1.anchor: قرأ عاصم وابن عامر: بربوة بفتح الراء، وفي المؤمنين (إلى ربوة)

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read aklahā lightly; the remaining readers use the heavier, original form.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو أكلها بالتخفيف، وقرأ الباقون بالتثقيل، وهو الأصل

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r3.speaker: السلمي
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r3.claim: The established readers read janna with jīm and nūn; al-Sulamī is reported with ḥāʾ and bāʾ instead.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r3.anchor: وجماعة القراء على جنة بالجيم والنون، وعن السلمي بالحاء والباء

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r4.claim: Ibtighāʾ is the verbal noun of ibtaghaytu: seeking; the related forms mean seeking something or helping someone seek it.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r4.anchor: الابتغاء: افتعال من ابتغيت الشيء أبغيه وأبتغيه: إذا طلبته، وبغيتك كذا

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r5.claim: Tathbīt comes from firmness and constancy; a thabt person does not waver in battle, while illness may keep someone from leaving.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r5.anchor: والتثبيت من قولهم: ثبت ثباتا، ورجل ثبت في الحرب إذا لم يزل، وأثبته السقم

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r6.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says an orchard with palms is called a janna, while one with grapevines is a firdaws; janna derives from concealment.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r6.anchor: قال الفراء: ما كان فيه نخل فهو جنة، وما كان فيه كرم فهو فردوس، وأصله من الجن وهو الستر

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r7.claim: Ribā means increase, and rabwa is elevated ground because it rises above its surroundings; the word has seven dialect forms.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r7.anchor: والربا: الزيادة، ربا الشيء إذا زاد، والربوة: العلو من الأرض لزيادته على غيره، وفيه سبع لغات

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r8.claim: With ḍamma, akl means food because it is eaten; with fatḥa, it is the verbal noun of eating.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r8.anchor: والأكل بالضم: الطعام؛ لأن من شأنه أن يؤكل، وبالفتح المضدر أكل يأكل أكلا

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r9.claim: Ṭall is fine-droplet rain, unlike the large, forceful drops of wābil.
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r9.anchor: والطل: المطر الصغير القطر، وهو خلاف الوابل؛ لأنه العظيم القطر الشديد الوقع

JISHUMI:v2p1031/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r10.claim: Ibtighāʾ is accusative as the object of yanfiqūn, or by omitting the preposition li-, meaning ‘for seeking.’
JISHUMI:v2p1031/r10.anchor: (ابتغاء) نصب ب (ينفقون)، وقيل: بنزع الخافضة أي لابتغاء

JISHUMI:v2p1033/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r1.claim: Worship must be done for God, seeking His pleasure and intending nearness to Him.
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r1.anchor: تدل الآية أن العبادة يجب أن تفعل لله تعالى، وطلب رضاه، وينوى التقرب إليه

JISHUMI:v2p1033/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r2.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r2.claim: The phrase also describes committing oneself to protect charity from corruption; the Qāḍī says these two qualities characterize sound charity and contrast with the two faults named for corrupt charity.
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r2.anchor: ويدل قوله: وتثبيتا أنهم يوطنون أنفسهم على حفظها مما يفسدها، قال القاضي

JISHUMI:v2p1033/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r3.claim: The verse encourages charity by promising multiplied reward.
JISHUMI:v2p1033/r3.anchor: وتدل آخر الآية على الترغيب في الصدقة من حيث وعد عليها بتضعيف الأجرة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p305/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p305/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p305/r1.claim: Bashshar’s simile forms one inseparable scene: dust and swords moving together resemble night as its stars dim and fall, not two separate pairwise comparisons.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p305/r1.anchor: أنه لم يرد أن يشبه النقع بالليل على حدة ، والأسياف بالكواكب على حدة . ولكنه أراد أن يشبه النقع والأسياف تجول فيه بالليل

DAMGHANI:v1p189/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r7.claim: Rabwah means level, elevated ground, a raised place or hill.
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r7.anchor: فوجه منها : الربوة المكان المستوي المرتفع قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi criticizes later writers for copying earlier books without reflecting on or investigating what they transmit.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r1.anchor: رأيت كل متأخر عن متقدم يحذو حذوه ، وينقل قوله مقلدا له

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r2.claim: He reports two works on Qur'anic wujūh attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas: one through ʿIkrima and another through ʿAli ibn Abi Talha.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r2.anchor: قد نسب كتاب في ' الوجوه والنظائر ' إلى ( عكرمة عن ) ابن عباس ' رضي الله عنهما ' وكتاب ) آخر إلى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r3.claim: He names al-Kalbi, Muqatil, al-Ansari, Matruh (with a transmitted book), al-Naqqash, al-Damighani, al-Banna, and Ibn al-Zaghuni as other compilers, and knows no further authors.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r3.anchor: وممن ألف كتب ' الوجوه والنظائر ' . الكلبي ، ومقاتل بن سليمان ، وأبو الفضل العباس بن الفضل الأنصاري

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r4.claim: He also cites Matruh ibn Muhammad's book, transmitted through ʿAbd Allah ibn Harun al-Hijazi from his father, and says he knows no other compilers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r4.anchor: وروى مطروح بن محمد بن شاكر عن عبد الله بن هارون الحجازي عن أبيه ، كتابا في ' الوجوه والنظائر ' ، وأبو بكر بن محمد بن الحسن النقاش

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r5.claim: Nazaʾir are identical word forms appearing in different Qur'anic places, while wujūh are the different meanings intended by those forms.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r5.anchor: فلفظ كل كلمة ذكرت في موضع نظير للفظ الكلمة المذكورة في الموضع الآخر ، وتفسير كل كلمة بمعنى غير معنى الآخرى هو الوجوه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r6.claim: The purpose of these books is to alert readers that a repeated word may carry a different meaning in each place.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r6.anchor: والذي أراد العلماء بوضع كتب الوجوه والنظائر أن يعرفوا السامع لهذه النظائر أن معانيها تختلف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r7.claim: Compilers sometimes stretch the category to include words whose meaning stays constant, such as town, village, city, man, and human being.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r7.anchor: وقد تجوز واضعوها فذكروا كلمة واحدة معناها في جميع المواضع واحد . كالبلد ، والقرية ، والمدينة ، والرجل ، والإنسان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r8.claim: He calls attempts to maximize the number of categories absurd, citing mistaken groupings of dhurriya and riba words, including “a garden on a height” under riba.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p81/r8.anchor: قصد أكثرهم كثرة الوجوه والأبواب ، فأتوا بالتهافت العجاب ، مثل أن ترجم بعضهم فقال : باب الذرية ، وذكر فيه ' ذرني ' ، ' وتذروه الرياح '

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines ifk as a lie because it is speech turned away from the truth.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الإفك : الكذب ، وسمي إفكا ، لأنه كلام قلب عن الحق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r2.claim: He derives ifk from turning someone away from a view; the overturned towns of Lot are called al-Muʾtafikāt, and a poem uses the term for being diverted from good conduct.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r2.anchor: وأصله من أفكت الرجل ، إذا صرفته عن رأي كان عليه ، ومنه قيل لمدائن قوم لوط : ' المؤتفكات ' لانقلابها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r3.claim: Ibn Faris gives the root sense as any matter diverted from its proper direction.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r3.anchor: قال ابن فارس : كل أمر صرف عن وجهه فقد أفك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says land is described as afikat when rain is diverted from it, leaving it without growth or good.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة ) : ويقال : أفكت الأرض

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r5.claim: One Qur'anic sense of ifk is a lie, as in the claims that something is ancient falsehood or their own fabrication.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r5.anchor: أحدها : الكذب . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأحقاف : ﴿ فسيقولون هذا إفك قديم ﴾ ، وفيها : ﴿ وذلك إفكهم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r6.claim: Another sense is turning people away from the truth, including being turned away from worshipping false gods.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r6.anchor: والثاني : الصرف . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأحقاف : ' أجئتنا لتأفكنا عن آلهتنا ) ^ ، وفي الذاريات : ^ ( يؤفك عنه من أفك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r7.claim: A third sense is overturning, used of the overturned towns of Lot.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r7.anchor: والثالث : القلب . ومنه قوله تعالى في براءة : ^ ( والمؤتفكات أتتهم رسلهم بالبينات ) ^ ، وفي النجم : ^ ( والمؤتفكة أهوى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r8.claim: A fourth sense is sorcery, as in Pharaoh's magicians swallowing what they cast.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r8.anchor: والرابع : السحر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف والشعراء : ^ ( فإذا هي تلقف ما يأفكون

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r9.claim: A fifth sense is slander, referring to the accusation against ʿAʾisha.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r9.anchor: والخامس : القذف . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور : ^ ( إن الذين جاؤوا بالإفك عصبة منكم ) ^ ، والمراد به : قذف عائشة رضي الله عنها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r10.speaker: بعض أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r10.claim: Some exegetes add a sixth sense, idols, as in the question about worshipping gods falsely besides God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p137/r10.anchor: وقد ألحق بعض أهل التفسير وجها سادسا : فقالوا والإفك الأصنام ومنه قوله تعالى في الصافات : ^ ( أئفكا آلهة دون الله تريدون

NASHR:v2p231/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p231/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم
NASHR:v2p231/r4.claim: Ibn Amir and Asim read the rāʾ of ربوة with fatḥa in al-Baqara and al-Mu'minun; the others use ḍamma.
NASHR:v2p231/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم بفتح الراء، وقرأ الباقون بضمها
